Issues.Title: perf(compiler-cli): track ambient global consumers by name and cache .d.ts global names
Issues.Body:
> [!NOTE]
> Stacked on #71823 and #71850. Only the last commit is new.

With #71823, every file that looks up an ambient global depends on every `.d.ts` file in `tsconfig.json` `files`. Editing any of them re-analyzes every consumer, and rebuilding the index re-parses all of them.

This change:
1. Records the global names each consumer looks up. When the index is rebuilt, only the files whose names now resolve to a different set of declaring `.d.ts` files are evicted.
   - A value change inside the same `.d.ts` (`declare const COMPILED: true` → `false`) leaves the candidates unchanged. The consumer still depends on that `.d.ts` directly, since it parsed it to evaluate the declaration, so the ordinary invalidation evicts it.
   - The diff and eviction run in `ensure_singletons_fresh`, before any per-file query reads the cache, rather than inside the index query. Every entry point that reads per-file analysis calls it first: `run_coordinator` (batch, delta, and watch rebuilds), `analyze_file_wire_blocking`, and `analyze_file_semantic_blocking`.
2. Caches the global names each `.d.ts` declares per file, so rebuilding the index after an edit only re-parses the edited files.

Emitted output doesn't change. The tests cover an unrelated `.d.ts` edit (no consumer evicted), a new declaration that changes a lookup (consumer evicted only by `ensure_singletons_fresh`), and a value change (consumer evicted through its dependency on the `.d.ts`), in both optimized and local wire modes.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "perf(compiler-cli): track ambient global consumers by name and cache .d.ts global names" (#71851)

Issues.Title: Router: with canceledNavigationResolution 'computed', cancelling the first navigation after a reload calls history.go() with a stale page id
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

router

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

With `canceledNavigationResolution: 'computed'`, cancelling (or erroring) the **first navigation after a page reload** makes the router call `history.go()` with a non-zero delta, so the browser jumps to an unrelated history entry instead of staying on the current one.

Cause (from `HistoryStateManager` in `_router-chunk.mjs`, 22.2.3):

- `currentPageId` starts at `0` in every new app instance.
- After a reload (or when the user comes back from another site via Back), `history.state` still carries the previous instance's `ɵrouterPageId` (for example `2`), and the initial navigation restores that state, so `browserPageId` returns `2`.
- If that initial navigation is cancelled (a guard returns `false`, a resolver errors, a `NavigationError` happens), `restoreHistory()` computes `targetPagePosition = this.currentPageId - this.browserPageId = 0 - 2` and calls `this.location.historyGo(-2)`.
- `lastSuccessfulId` is still `-1` at that point: there is no previous router-owned position to go back to, so any non-zero `historyGo` is wrong. If the first navigation keeps failing (e.g. a guard that rejects on startup), the app walks back through the history one batch at a time.

### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

No StackBlitz yet; minimal steps:

1. `provideRouter(routes, withRouterConfig({ canceledNavigationResolution: 'computed' }))` with routes `/a`, `/b`, `/c`, where `/c` has a `canActivate` guard that returns `false` when a flag (e.g. a `sessionStorage` key) is set.
2. Navigate in-app `/a` → `/b` → `/c`. `history.state.ɵrouterPageId` is now `2` on the `/c` entry.
3. Set the flag and reload the page on `/c`.

Expected: the cancelled initial navigation leaves the history position unchanged (at most resets the URL of the current entry).
Actual: the router calls `history.go(-2)` and the browser ends up on the entry before `/a`.

The same happens when the initial navigation fails for other reasons (startup error in a guard, a resolver throwing), and when the user returns with Back from another site to an entry that carries a page id.

### Please provide the exception or error you saw

```true
No exception; the browser silently navigates to another history entry (history.go(0 - restoredPageId)).
```

### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`)

```true
Angular: 22.2.3 (router 22.2.3)
Browser: Chrome (latest stable)
```

### Anything else?

Possible fixes:
- When the initial navigation restores a state with `ɵrouterPageId`, initialize `currentPageId` from it (so `currentPageId - browserPageId === 0` until a navigation succeeds), or
- In `restoreHistory()` for `'computed'`, skip `historyGo` when no navigation has succeeded yet (`lastSuccessfulId === -1`) and only reset the URL of the current entry.

Our workaround is to never cancel the first navigation: guards return `NEVER` (hold the navigation) instead of `false`/`UrlTree` on startup failures, which is not obvious and changes first-navigation semantics.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "Router: with canceledNavigationResolution 'computed', cancelling the first navigation after a reload calls history.go() with a stale page id" (#71849)

Issues.Title: build: update pnpm to v11.28.11 (22.2.x)
Issues.Body:
This PR contains the following updates: | Package | Change | [Age](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Adoption](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Passing](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Confidence](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | [pnpm](https://pnpm.io) ([source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/tree/HEAD/pnpm/npm/pnpm)) | [`11.28.9` → `11.28.11`](https://renovatebot.com/diffs/npm/pnpm/11.28.9/11.28.11) | ![age](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/age/npm/pnpm/11.28.11?slim=true) | ![adoption](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/adoption/npm/pnpm/11.28.11?slim=true) | ![passing](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/compatibility/npm/pnpm/11.28.9/11.28.11?slim=true) | ![confidence](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/confidence/npm/pnpm/11.28.9/11.28.11?slim=true) | --- - [ ] If you want to rebase/retry this PR, check this box --- ### Release Notes
pnpm/pnpm (pnpm) ### [`v11.28.11`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v11.28.11): pnpm 11.28.11 [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v11.28.10...v11.28.11) pnpm 11.28.11 fixes frozen installs with `excludeLinksFromLockfile`, `pnpm link` in workspaces, `pnpm deploy` with dangling symlinks, and `verifyDepsBeforeRun` starting needless installs. ##### Patch Changes ##### Installing packages - `pnpm deploy` now keeps a symlink in the project whose target is missing from the source, such as a link into a `node_modules` directory that was removed after the build. Deploy used to fail with `ENOENT` on such a link [#​17571](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17571). - A package with `bundledDependencies` and a build script now keeps its bundled dependencies when it is restored from the side-effects cache [#​17523](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17523). - `pnpm install` now links the runtime that an earlier `pnpm install --no-runtime` skipped [#​17542](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17542). - Commands of a package whose `bin` paths contain excess parent directory segments, such as `../dist/cli.js`, are no longer missing. Such paths now resolve inside the package [#​17586](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17586). - Generated POSIX shell shims now quote their paths, so shell special characters in a path stay literal. - A repeat `pnpm install` now rewrites the bin shims after `extendNodePath` changes. Before, it reported "Already up to date" and the shims kept the `NODE_PATH` of the previous setting. ##### Lockfile and resolution - `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` now accepts the lockfile it wrote with `excludeLinksFromLockfile` and `linkWorkspacePackages` on, when a project depends on a workspace package through a plain version range or a `catalog:` entry. It used to fail with `ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE`. - `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm approve-builds`, and `pnpm rebuild` now accept a lockfile that resolves a `*` dependency to a prerelease `latest` version. pnpm wrote such a lockfile and then reported it as outdated [#​17594](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17594). - Packages from the default registry keep plain lockfile keys, even when a prefix such as `npmjs` points at the registry set as `registry`. A dependency written with such a prefix shares the plain entry of the same package. The next install rewrites keys that earlier versions qualified this way [#​17575](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17575). - Relative local paths in root `overrides` now resolve from the workspace root when each project has its own lockfile [#​17691](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17691). Installing a local directory dependency no longer fails when another project's install is writing a lockfile in that directory. - Peer deduplication no longer gives a project different copies of a dependency across direct and transitive paths when an optional peer has no provider [#​17666](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17666). - A Node.js version range such as `>=26.13`, for example in `devEngines.runtime`, now resolves to the newest stable release that satisfies it. pnpm picks a prerelease only when no stable release matches [#​17516](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17516). ##### verifyDepsBeforeRun - With `verifyDepsBeforeRun`, `pnpm run` and `pnpm exec` now report dependencies as out of date after a dependency is added to the `package.json` of a local directory dependency, such as `"lib": "file:../lib"`. Before, the command ran without the new dependency installed. - `verifyDepsBeforeRun` no longer reports dependencies as out of sync when only the `version` field of a single-project repository changed [#​17560](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17560). The same holds for a workspace project that no dependency can resolve to. A script run after such a change no longer starts an install first. ##### pnpm link - In a workspace, `pnpm link ` now adds the `link:` dependency to the `package.json` of the project where the command runs, not to the workspace root's `package.json`. The link is created in that project's `node_modules`, as documented. The override is still written to the root `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. - `pnpm link` with several paths now records every linked package in the `overrides` of `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. Some of them could be missing before. - `pnpm link` now fails without changing `package.json` or `pnpm-workspace.yaml` when the linked package's name is not a valid npm package name. It used to write that name to both files, which made every later install fail [#​17475](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17475). ##### pnpm update - `pnpm update` with only negated selectors, such as `pnpm update '!foo'`, now leaves the dependencies listed in `update.ignoreDeps` unchanged [pnpm/tasks#243](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/243). - `pnpm update --depth 0` without selectors now does nothing when every direct dependency is listed in `update.ignoreDeps`. Before, it failed with `ERR_PNPM_NO_PACKAGE_IN_DEPENDENCIES` [pnpm/tasks#251](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/251). ##### Store and self-update - `pnpm store prune` now keeps packages linked from a configured modules directory [pnpm/tasks#230](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/230). - `pnpm store status` no longer reports untouched packages as modified when the global virtual store is enabled. If the installed global-store layout cannot be verified, the command reports `ERR_PNPM_STORE_STATUS_UNVERIFIABLE` and asks for a reinstall [#​17631](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17631). - `pnpm store add` now fails right away with `ERR_PNPM_FROZEN_STORE_WRITE` when `frozenStore` is enabled. It used to retry each download for minutes before failing, or fail with a SQLite error on an empty store. - `pnpm self-update` now reinstalls a cached engine if its executable cannot run. This repairs shared store entries damaged by an earlier install [#​17582](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17582). ##### Platinum Sponsors
##### Gold Sponsors
### [`v11.28.10`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v11.28.10): pnpm 11.28.10 [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v11.28.9...v11.28.10) pnpm 11.28.10 stops `pnpm store prune` from deleting other stores when `cacheDir` points to their parent directory. It also fixes globally installed commands that load hoisted dependencies, and repeat installs that missed changes to local dependencies. ##### Patch Changes ##### Installing packages - `pnpm store prune` preserves other stores and global package data when `cacheDir` points to their parent directory. - Commands installed with `pnpm add --global` now find the dependencies that pnpm hoists for their package. A package that loads a dependency it does not declare, such as a native addon's platform-specific package, failed with "Cannot find module". Reinstall such a package with `pnpm add --global` to update its existing command [#​17503](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17503). - `pnpm prune --prod` no longer fails with `ERR_PNPM_EXDEV` when `node_modules` was copied from an earlier Docker build stage [#​17424](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17424). - `pnpm install` now retries a Node.js runtime zip download when the connection drops partway through. A download that still fails names its URL. Before, a single dropped connection ended the install with `terminated` [#​17411](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17411). - With the global virtual store, a change to a dependency of one package in a dependency cycle now gives every package in that cycle a new directory. Before, the other packages kept their directories and still linked the old copy of the changed package, so the project could load two copies of it [#​17466](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17466). Packages in a dependency cycle, and packages that depend on one, move to new global virtual store directories once after this update. Those that run a build miss the side-effects cache once. - `pnpm install` and `pnpm rebuild` now refresh privately hoisted `.bin` shims in `node_modules/.pnpm/node_modules/.bin` after a dependency build replaces a script target with a native executable [#​17402](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17402). - The Node.js `latest` selector now chooses the newest stable release [#​17490](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17490). - The standalone `@pnpm/exe` builds now embed Node.js 26.13.0. ##### Repeat installs and lockfiles - `pnpm install` now resolves a local directory again after its `package.json` changes when an override or a package extension adds it to the dependencies of a registry package. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` fails on a lockfile that still records the old dependencies of such a directory [#​17486](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17486). - With `injectWorkspacePackages` and per-project lockfiles, `pnpm install` now updates a project's lockfile when a local tarball that an injected workspace project depends on is replaced. The project's lockfile kept the old version and integrity before. - `pnpm install` now detects a change to a local tarball or directory that only a pnpmfile `readPackage` hook depends on. A repeat install reported "Already up to date" and kept the old contents before [pnpm/tasks#227](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/227). - `pnpm install` now relinks a `workspace:` or `link:` dependency whose link was deleted from `node_modules`. It used to report "Already up to date" and leave the link missing [#​17485](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17485). - Merging git branch lockfiles now keeps a workspace project whose directory is named `__proto__`. It was dropped from the merged lockfile before [pnpm/tasks#59](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/59). ##### Adding and publishing packages - `pnpm add` no longer rewrites a catalog entry set to the dist-tag that the dependency resolves through. For example, an entry `beta` stays `beta` after `pnpm add foo@beta` or `pnpm add foo`. Before, the entry was replaced with the version the tag pointed to [pnpm/tasks#225](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/225). - `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` now always include the binary file declared by a string `bin` field in `package.json`, even when `files` or `.npmignore` would otherwise exclude it. - When the version or range given to `pnpm unpublish` matches every published version, the error now says so and shows the same command with `--force`. It suggested running `pnpm unpublish @`, the command that had just failed. ##### Running commands - Every command, including `pnpm --version`, `pnpm self-update`, and invocations with unknown flags, now applies the same `packageManager` and `devEngines.packageManager` settings when switching to the pinned pnpm version or recording it in `pnpm-lock.yaml`. `--config.` flags and `lockfileDir` now reach the version switch and lockfile sync on every entry point. Unreadable settings in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` or the global `config.yaml` that do not affect the pin decision no longer block the version switch [pnpm/tasks#222](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/222). - On Windows, the shell shim of a `.cmd` or `.bat` bin now runs it under Git Bash when MSYS argument conversion is off, such as with `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` or `MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL='*'`. The shim used to start an interactive cmd.exe prompt [#​17480](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17480). - `pnx` and `pnpm create` now run the command in the directory selected by `--dir` or `--workspace-root`. Without either flag, the command still runs in the directory pnpm was started in. - The error for a dependency with an invalid name in a project's manifest now names the project's directory. It used to say only "The current package", which did not tell which workspace project to fix [#​17475](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17475). ##### Platinum Sponsors
##### Gold Sponsors

### [`v12.18.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.18.0): pnpm 12.18

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.17.0...v12.18.0)

pnpm 12.18.0 packs, publishes, and installs packages with platform variants on pnpr registries. It also adds per-skill approval of agent skills and `pnpm store add` for offline installs from downloaded tarballs. Repeat installs and `verifyDepsBeforeRun` no longer read the `package.json` of unchanged workspace projects. The release fixes several peer dependency resolution bugs too.

##### Minor Changes

##### Agent skills

- pnpm now names the link to a dependency's agent skill after the skill alone. A skill that the `@acme/kit` package ships in `skills/auth/` is linked as `.claude/skills/auth`, not `.claude/skills/pnpm-@acme+kit-auth`. The next install replaces links with the old names. pnpm lists the linked skills in a `# pnpm` block of each agent skill directory's `.gitignore` [#​17455](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/discussions/17455).

  When two approved packages ship a skill of the same name, or the name is already taken in an agent skill directory, pnpm links the skill as `pnpm-<package>-<skill>`. Before, the install failed.

- `pnpm approve` now asks which agent skills to link when a package ships more than one. pnpm records the chosen skills as a list, such as `permissions.<pkg>.skills: [guide, migrate]`, and does not offer the other skills for approval again. The first time a project approves a skill, `pnpm approve` also asks which agent directories to link skills into, and records the answer under `skills.dirs`.

- pnpm links agent skills nested in category directories, such as `skills/engineering/implement/SKILL.md`, up to three levels below `skills/`. Before, it linked only the skills directly under `skills/`.

##### Platform variants

These features need a registry declared with `serverType: pnpr`.

- `pnpm pack` packs one archive per entry of `publishConfig.variants`, each platform variant as `<name>-<version>~<tag>.tgz`. `pnpm pack --variant <target>` packs only the archive whose entry lists that target. `pnpm pack --json` prints the `integrity` and `size` of every archive it writes.

- `pnpm publish` publishes a package's `publishConfig.variants`. pnpm uploads every archive before the publish request that references them. Publishing variants to any other registry is refused unless `--no-variants` is given, which publishes only the archive that targets `any`.

- `pnpm publish --upload-variant <target>` uploads the archive of one `publishConfig.variants` entry to the registry's staging area and prints `<target>=<integrity>`. `pnpm publish --variant-integrity <target>=<integrity>` then publishes the version from archives that other jobs uploaded. With `--recursive`, each value names its package as `<name>~<target>=<integrity>`.

- `pnpm publish -r --batch` now uploads each package archive on its own request and skips archives the registry already holds, so the batch request no longer grows with the archives it publishes. A batch of more than 256 packages still carries every archive inline. Packages with `publishConfig.variants` can be published in a batch. A batch with variants that would reference more than 256 archives on one registry fails with `ERR_PNPM_BATCH_PUBLISH_TOO_MANY_ARCHIVES` [pnpm/tasks#244](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/244).

- `pnpm publish --provenance` signs one statement that names every archive of a version with `publishConfig.variants`. A platform variant's archive is named by the version's package URL with a `variant` qualifier.

- Rerunning `pnpm publish` after the version was already published now succeeds when the published version is the same release. pnpm compares the archives, the provenance statement when the rerun signs one, and the dist-tag. When the published version differs, the publish fails with `ERR_PNPM_PUBLISHED_RELEASE_DIFFERS`, which names what differs.

- pnpm installs the platform variant of a package that fits the host, or the package's own archive when none does. The lockfile records every variant. A version published with variants only, and no archive for other hosts, installs on a host one of the variants fits. On any other host, an optional dependency is skipped, and any other dependency fails with an error that lists the platforms the version is published for.

- `supportedArchitectures` platform lists accept platform tags, the same tags `publishConfig.variants` entries name. An entry can state floors and an ABI, such as `linux-x64-manylinux_2_28`, `darwin-arm64-macos_14_0`, `linux-x64-napi8` or `linux-x64-node127`, and any Node.js OS and CPU, such as `freebsd-x64`. The spellings accepted before still work.

- With `supportedArchitectures` set, pnpm also fetches into the store the variants that the other listed platforms need, when it downloads a package with platform variants.

##### pnpr registries

- pnpm downloads less metadata from a registry declared with `serverType: pnpr`. A large package document leaves out the manifests of rarely picked versions, and pnpm fetches one only when it picks that version. In a benchmark that resolves 787 packages, the package documents shrank from 30.3 MB to 2.5 MB gzipped. pnpm caches these documents in `v12/metadata-pnpr`, and the `pnpm cache` commands cover them.

  pnpm warns when a registry that is not declared `serverType: pnpr` turns out to be pnpr. For a registry declared `serverType: pnpr`, a `minimumReleaseAge` longer than 30 days fails with `ERR_PNPM_UNSUPPORTED_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE`.

- `pnpm publish` sends release notes to registries declared with `serverType: pnpr`. A package's notes are the section for its version in `CHANGELOG.md`, or the notes that `pnpm version -r` composed from change intents. `--release-notes <file>` gives the notes from a file, and `--no-release-notes` sends none. `--publication-name` names a release published with `--batch`.

  In a workspace that uses pnpm's versioning, `pnpm version -r --release-notes <file>` puts a summary above the composed notes of the release.

  `pnpm view <pkg>@<version> releaseNotes`, `pnpm outdated --notes`, and `pnpm update --interactive` show the release notes from these registries.

##### Store and hooks

- `pnpm store add` now prepares the store for offline installs from package tarballs downloaded some other way. After `pnpm store add ./tarballs/*.tgz`, `pnpm install --offline --frozen-lockfile` installs each registry package whose lockfile entry pins one of those tarballs [#​2978](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/2978).

- Custom pnpmfile fetchers can use `fetchers.gitHostedTarball`, `fetchers.git`, and `fetchers.binary` [pnpm/tasks#191](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/191).

##### Patch Changes

##### Installing packages

- Running `node` or `pnpm install` in a project that pins a Node.js version pnpm has not downloaded yet no longer hangs when a `globalPnpmfile` is configured [#​17530](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17530).

- `pnpm install` with `enableGlobalVirtualStore` no longer fails on Windows for a dependency from a named registry, such as `gh:` or `npmjs:` [#​17665](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17665).

- Concurrent installs that share a global virtual store no longer fail with `ERR_PNPM_CMD_SHIM_SYMLINK_BIN` when they link the same executable at the same time [#​17587](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17587).

- `pnpm install` and `pnpm ci` now succeed when dependency skills are approved but no agent skill directory exists. The skills stay unlinked until a directory exists [#​17574](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17574).

- Commands run from a workspace package now use the same default store as the workspace root. Before, `pnpm add` in a package could fail with `ERR_PNPM_UNEXPECTED_STORE` when the workspace root was its own mount point and the home store was on another volume, as in a sandbox or a container.

  A workspace installed with the old behavior may need one `pnpm install --force` from the workspace root.

- `pnpm deploy` now keeps a symlink in the project whose target is missing from the source, such as a link into a `node_modules` directory that was removed after the build. Deploy used to drop such a link silently [#​17571](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17571).

- `pnpm install` now links the runtime that an earlier `pnpm install --no-runtime` skipped, and `pnpm install --no-runtime` removes a runtime that an earlier install linked [#​17542](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17542).

- With `enableGlobalVirtualStore`, `pnpm install` again runs a dependency's build scripts in a project whose global virtual store slot another project already built, unless the side-effects cache has build output to restore for it. A build that writes only outside its own package, such as a git hook installer, now takes effect in every project [#​17526](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17526).

- Commands of a package whose `bin` paths contain excess parent directory segments, such as `../dist/cli.js`, are no longer missing. Such paths now resolve inside the package [#​17586](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17586).

- Generated POSIX shell shims now quote their paths, so shell special characters in a path stay literal.

##### Lockfile and local paths

- Packages from the default registry keep plain lockfile keys, even when a prefix such as `npmjs` points at the registry set as `registry`. A dependency written with such a prefix shares the plain entry of the same package. The next install rewrites keys that earlier versions qualified this way [#​17575](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17575).

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm approve-builds`, and `pnpm rebuild` now accept a lockfile that resolves a `*` dependency to a prerelease `latest` version. pnpm wrote such a lockfile and then reported it as outdated [#​17594](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17594).

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` now accepts a lockfile written with `excludeLinksFromLockfile` and `linkWorkspacePackages` on, when a project depends on a workspace package through a `catalog:` entry. It used to fail with `ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE`.

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` no longer rejects a freshly generated lockfile when `addMissingPeerTypes` is enabled and an injected workspace package has peer dependencies [#​17668](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17668).

- Relative local paths in root `overrides` now resolve from the workspace root when each project has its own lockfile [#​17691](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17691).

  Installing a local directory dependency no longer fails when another project's install is writing a lockfile in that directory.

- Relative local paths in root catalogs now resolve for dependencies and peers [#​17690](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17690).

- `pnpm install` now resolves auto-installed relative `workspace:` and `file:` peers from the directory of the package that declares them [#​17676](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17676), [#​17689](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17689).

- `pnpm dedupe --check` leaves `pnpm-lock.yaml` untouched while it looks for deduplication changes. If `configDependencies` changed since the last install, the check keeps the lockfile they sync, as `pnpm install` does [#​17628](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17628).

- `pnpm dedupe --check` no longer fails when the only difference is the integrity of a locked version that the registry now reports with a stronger algorithm, such as a `sha512` integrity replacing the `sha1` shasum it reported when the lockfile was written [#​17692](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17692).

##### Peer dependencies

- Peer deduplication no longer gives a project different copies of a dependency across direct and transitive paths when an optional peer has no provider [#​17666](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17666).

- Dependencies no longer bind to another project's peer variant when the provider has nested peers, including providers that finish resolving later [#​17593](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17593).

- Re-resolving a lockfile no longer preserves optional peer bindings from other projects when no provider is in scope [#​17592](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17592).

- `pnpm peers check` warns when a required peer is resolved without a provider declared by the project or its dependency ancestors, with `autoInstallPeers: false` and `dedupePeerDependents: true`. These warnings do not change the command's exit code or cause `strictPeerDependencies` failures.

##### Speed and memory

- `pnpm install`, and `pnpm run` and `pnpm exec` with `verifyDepsBeforeRun`, no longer read the `package.json` of workspace projects whose files did not change since the last install. This also holds with a pnpmfile, `configDependencies`, or `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false`. In an up-to-date workspace with `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false`, `pnpm install` no longer runs the install of each project [pnpm/tasks#256](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/256).

- A recursive `pnpm run` or `pnpm exec` with `verifyDepsBeforeRun` set no longer reads every `package.json` in the workspace once per project when `sharedWorkspaceLockfile` is `false`. In a 300-project workspace, `pnpm -r exec true` went from 490 ms to 42 ms [pnpm/tasks#256](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/256).

- `pnpm install` makes fewer `stat` calls when it hardlinks files from the store, as few as 12.7.0 made [#​17543](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17543).

- Picking versions from registry metadata uses less temporary memory.

##### verifyDepsBeforeRun and repeat installs

- With `verifyDepsBeforeRun`, `pnpm run` and `pnpm exec` now report dependencies as out of date after a dependency is added to the `package.json` of a local directory dependency, such as `"lib": "file:../lib"`. Before, the command ran without the new dependency installed.

- `verifyDepsBeforeRun` no longer reports a `file:` directory dependency as out of date after an edit to `package.json` that leaves its dependencies unchanged [#​17697](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17697).

- `verifyDepsBeforeRun` no longer reports dependencies as out of sync when only the `version` field of a single-project repository changed [#​17560](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17560). The same holds for a workspace project that no dependency can resolve to. A script run after such a change no longer starts an install first.

- A repeat `pnpm install` now rewrites the bin shims after `extendNodePath` changes. Before, it reported "Already up to date" and the shims kept the `NODE_PATH` of the previous setting.

##### Adding and updating dependencies

- `pnpm add <pkg>` without a version now saves the range that the other workspace projects declare for the package, or the one a matching override sets. A `catalog:` reference still comes first, and the `tag` setting is used only when none of these exists [pnpm/tasks#191](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/191).

- `pnpm update` with only negated selectors, such as `pnpm update '!foo'`, now leaves the dependencies listed in `update.ignoreDeps` unchanged. Negated `crate:` and `pypi:` selectors, such as `!crate:sha2`, now exclude that dependency and update the rest [pnpm/tasks#243](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/243).

- `pnpm update --latest` keeps three kinds of Cargo dependencies where they are, unless the crate is named on the command line. Before, it moved each one to the newest release and left a workspace that did not build.

  - A renamed dependency, such as `tower-0-4 = { package = "tower", version = "0.4" }`, stays within its requirement if the workspace also declares the crate under its own name.
  - A crate replaced through `[patch.crates-io]` keeps its version, with a warning.
  - A crate whose newest release is older than its current version, such as a prerelease newer than the latest stable release, keeps its version, with a warning. Only an explicit version, such as `pnpm update crate:foo@1`, moves it back.

  Other new major versions are still selected and may need code changes.

- `pnpm update` now keeps a Cargo dependency at its current version, with a warning, if the new version lacks a feature the workspace enables on it. If the crate is named on the command line, as in `pnpm update --latest crate:sha2`, the update fails with an error that names the missing features.

- `pnpm update` now keeps the operator of every existing Cargo requirement, so `~1.0.0` is updated to `~1.1.0`, and an exact `=` requirement stays exact unless the selector gives a range, such as `crate:foo@^2`. The `savePrefix` and `saveExact` settings apply only to new Cargo dependencies. Saved Cargo requirements omit build metadata.

- `pnpm update` now updates a Cargo dependency whose inline table spans several lines, such as one with a multi-line `features` array. It failed with "its Cargo.toml dependency declaration is not a string or single-line inline table".

- `pnpm update` no longer applies the `savePrefix` and `saveExact` settings to Python requirements. A `savePrefix` such as `^` made `pnpm update` fail in a project with Python dependencies.

  `pnpm update` now keeps the precision of a `~=` requirement, so `~=1.0` is updated to `~=1.5` and still allows any 1.x release. With `--latest`, a `==1.*` requirement is updated to `==2.*`.

##### Store

- `pnpm store prune` now keeps packages linked from a configured modules directory [pnpm/tasks#230](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/230).

- `pnpm store prune` now removes aliases of pruned packages.

- `pnpm store status` no longer reports untouched packages as modified when the global virtual store is enabled. If the installed global-store layout cannot be verified, the command reports `ERR_PNPM_STORE_STATUS_UNVERIFIABLE` and asks for a reinstall [#​17631](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17631).

- `pnpm store add` now fails with `ERR_PNPM_FROZEN_STORE_WRITE` when `frozenStore` is enabled. It used to write package files into the read-only store without recording them, so no install could use them.

- `pnpm cat-index <name>@<version>` no longer shows the index of a package whose name differs only in letter case.

##### Other commands and settings

- `pnpm link` now fails without changing `package.json` or `pnpm-workspace.yaml` when the linked package's name is not a valid npm package name. It used to write that name to both files, which made every later install fail [#​17475](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17475).

- `pnpm link <dir>` now resolves a relative `<dir>` against the current directory. In a directory without a `package.json`, such as a workspace's `packages` folder, `pnpm link .` used to link the nearest project above it into itself [#​17475](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17475).

- A Node.js version range such as `>=26.13`, for example in `devEngines.runtime`, now resolves to the newest stable release that satisfies it. pnpm picks a prerelease only when no stable release matches [#​17516](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17516).

- Switching to the pnpm version a project pins no longer writes a temporary `_tmp_*` file into the project directory, which file watchers reported on every command [#​17681](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17681).

- pnpm now reads the `linkWorkspacePackages`, `injectWorkspacePackages`, `extendNodePath`, `frozenStore`, and `optimisticRepeatInstall` settings from `PNPM_CONFIG_*` environment variables, such as `PNPM_CONFIG_LINK_WORKSPACE_PACKAGES=true`. `--config.extend-node-path` now applies too.

- Recursive scripts run with `--sequential` or `--workspace-concurrency=1` print GitHub Actions log groups again [#​17629](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17629).

- When `pnpm docs` cannot open a browser, the URL it prints no longer includes the query string or the fragment.

Issues.Title: fix(zone.js): keep the Node.js async context in microtasks
Issues.Body:
Previously, `then()` recorded only `Zone.current`, and every promise reaction in the process is drained from one shared microtask. Each reaction, the task hooks around it and the reporting of its errors ran in the async context of whatever scheduled that microtask, so on the server `AsyncLocalStorage.getStore()` could return the store of another request. Since `NgZone` runs change detection from those hooks, a whole tick could run as the wrong request.

Capture the async context when the callback is registered and run the task inside it, as Node.js recommends for custom thenables. Set `__Zone_disable_asyncContext` to opt out.

Fixes #71825

Issues.Title: zone.js: Promise reactions cause cross request `AsyncLocalStorage` context leakage in SSR
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

zone.js

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description


With zone.js loaded on the server, `AsyncLocalStorage.getStore()` can return the store of a different SSR request.

zone.js replaces the global `Promise`. In `then()` it saves `Zone.current`, but not Node's async context promise
 https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/124bf448091d0b2314275ca9bed12d82b3b7ef7e/packages/zone.js/lib/common/promise.ts#L545-L550

The reactions then go into one queue for the whole process, and the queue is drained from a single native microtask, scheduled by whatever queued first 

https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/124bf448091d0b2314275ca9bed12d82b3b7ef7e/packages/zone.js/lib/zone-impl.ts#L1513-L1565

Node runs that microtask in the async context of the code that scheduled it. So when two requests have reactions in the same drain, all of them run with the first request's store. `Zone.current` is still right for each task, and `inject(REQUEST)` was right in every render I measured. What's wrong is Node's async context, which is what `AsyncLocalStorage` reads.

A lot of server code finds the current request that way: express-http-context, a pino logger with a request context, OpenTelemetry's context manager, Sentry. In my test app an interceptor forwards the user's token from express-http-context, and 20 concurrent renders called the backend with the same user's token.

Code in the app always goes through `then()`, because with zone.js in `polyfills` the CLI compiles `async`/`await` to generators over the global `Promise`. In both apps below, the zone.js server bundle has no native `await` left, while the zoneless build of the same source keeps 70 (Angular 22) and 80 (Angular 21).

```text
node v24.16.0, zone.js 0.16.3

test                          request   Zone.current   als.getStore()  verdict
A same-turn .then()           victim    req-victim     victim          ok
A same-turn .then()           attacker  req-attacker   victim          LEAK
B shared in-flight promise    victim    req-victim     victim          ok
B shared in-flight promise    attacker  req-attacker   victim          LEAK
C still wrong 3 hops later    victim    req-victim     victim          ok
C still wrong 3 hops later    attacker  req-attacker   victim          LEAK
D native await                victim    <root>         victim          ok
D native await                attacker  <root>         attacker        ok

AsyncLocalStorage store from another request: 3/8
Zone.current from another request:            0/8 (2 are <root> after native await)
```

With 0.16.3 it's the same on Node 20.19.5, 22.23.4, 24.16.0 and 26.13.0,


Two renders have to be waiting on the same pending work. 

| | what both renders wait on | what the app needs | first requests of a process | after warm-up |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | the SSR manifest's `import()` of `main.server.mjs` and the index HTML | nothing | yes | no |
| 2 | the router's `loadComponent` | a lazy route that reads the identity | yes | no |
| 3 | the chunk of a `@defer` block with a `hydrate` trigger | that block, with incremental hydration on | yes | no |
| 4 | every `import()`, once an async ESM loader hook is registered | `@sentry/node` on Node 22 | yes | yes |
| 5 | a request shared through a `useValue` provider | that provider | yes | yes |

In all five, the same app without zone.js is correct. The other pieces only decide when two renders end up in the same drain.

Angular 22.2.4, on the Node versions it supports. `/account`, 20 concurrent renders with their own session cookie, first requests of a new process. Distinct bearer tokens the backend received:

| | Node 22.23.4 | 24.22.2 | 26.13.0 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `@sentry/node` 11.10.0 with `--import`, no cache (4) | 1 | 20 | 20 |
| `useValue` cache (5) | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| neither | 20 | 20 | 20 |
| zoneless, with Sentry or with the cache | 20 | 20 | 20 |

The Sentry row has no cache and no shared state in the app, and it gives the same result with the manifest's imports loaded before the server starts listening. On Linux with Node 22.22.3, which is Angular 22's minimum, it's also 1 token for 20 renders. It keeps happening after warm-up: over three runs on 22.23.4 the backend got 14 to 16 distinct tokens for 100 renders, and 84 to 86 log lines had the wrong user.

Sentry uses the synchronous `module.registerHooks()` only on Node 24.13+ and 25.1+ (`@sentry/server-runtime-injection/build/cjs/register.js:28-34`). On older versions it registers two asynchronous `module.register()` hooks, and `@angular/ssr` imports the index HTML on every render (`ssr.mjs:1172`), so there is always an `import()` that two renders can wait on.

The cache in row 5 holds public settings and is shared on purpose: one `HttpClient` call, `shareReplay`, and `await firstValueFrom(...)` in each render. What crosses is the identity, not the cached value. After warm-up it was 69 tokens for 100 renders on 22.23.4 and 81 on 26.13.0.

The application doesn't have to use `AsyncLocalStorage` itself. I removed all the identity code and kept only OpenTelemetry's zero-code agent and the cache, and the backend received 1 trace id for 20 renders, on 22.23.4 and on 26.13.0. OpenTelemetry's context manager reads the store in `active()` (`AsyncLocalStorageContextManager.cjs:41`).

Cases 1 to 3 are inside Angular, and they need Node older than 22.18.0. Angular 21.2.26 on Node 22.17.1, 3 new processes with 20 concurrent requests each, renders that read another request's identity:

| route | zone.js | zoneless |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `/account`, identity read in a resolver (1) | 57/60 | 0/60 |
| `/profile`, lazy, identity read in the component (2) | 57/60 | 0/60 |
| `/` and `/settings`, `@defer (hydrate on …)` panel (3) | 30/33 | 0/33 |

Same numbers on 20.19.5 and 22.16.0. On `/account` without the cache, the backend received 1 distinct token for 20 renders and pino logged 19 of 20 lines under the wrong user. These three happen in the first requests of a process, after a deploy or a restart.

They stop at 22.18.0 because a new request arrives in an I/O callback, so it can only join an `import()` that is still pending after a turn of the event loop. One cold chunk import spans 11 to 18 turns on 22.17.1 and none on 22.18.0, the release with nodejs/node#57419 (*esm: syncify default path of `ModuleLoader.load`*). That covers Angular 21 on Node 20 and on Node 22 before 22.18.0.


### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

https://github.com/SkyZeroZx/zone-als-leak

 ### Expected behavior

A reaction runs in the async context where `then()` was called, as it does with native promises, so each request's `AsyncLocalStorage.getStore()` returns its own store. Node's docs ask the same of a custom thenable implementation [async_context, Troubleshooting: Context loss](https://nodejs.org/api/async_context.html#troubleshooting-context-loss).

### Anything else?


It also works the other way around. If the attacker's request is the one that starts the shared fetch, the other renders in that burst run as the attacker: they load the attacker's account with the attacker's token, and whatever they write is recorded as the attacker.

This reminds me in part of [GHSA-68x2-mx4q-78m7](https://github.com/angular/angular/security/advisories/GHSA-68x2-mx4q-78m7), where concurrent SSR requests could also end up with another request's data. There it was the global platform injector; here it is Node's async context.

Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "build: update cross-repo angular dependencies (main)" (#34647)

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): forward the poll and progress options to the karma build setup
Issues.Body:
The karma builder schema documents the `poll` and `progress` options, but the application build it starts never receives them: `--no-progress` still logs build progress and `poll` does not switch the file watcher to polling. The legacy webpack-based karma builder honored both options.

Forward both values to the build options. No new test since both are pass-through options; the package unit tests cover the compilation of the changed setup.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(@angular/build): forward the poll and progress options to the karma build setup" (#34654)

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/cli): report the worktree-local cache in `ng cache info`
Issues.Body:
In a Git worktree the development server keeps its Vite cache in the worktree's own cache directory while the configured path resolves to the shared cache of the main checkout. `ng cache clean` removes both since the `getCacheConfig` localPath addition, but `ng cache info` still reports only the shared path and its size, so the cache that the development server actually writes to in that checkout is invisible.

Print the local path and its size when it differs from the shared path. Outside of a worktree both paths are the same and the output is unchanged.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(@angular/cli): report the worktree-local cache in `ng cache info`" (#34653)

Issues.Title: refactor(@angular/ssr): remove unused constructUrl helper
Issues.Body: Remove the `constructUrl` function, which was added in 61a027dba7 without a caller and has never been referenced anywhere since. It is not exported from the package entry points and does not appear in the public API golden.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "refactor(@angular/ssr): remove unused constructUrl helper" (#34649)

Issues.Title: refactor(@angular-devkit/schematics): remove unused code and exports
Issues.Body: Remove the `FallbackEngineHost` and its supporting types, which have not been referenced anywhere since the devkit repository was merged in 44086c60ff and were never exported from the `tools` entry point, and remove the `export` keyword from four exception classes that are only thrown within their defining file and are not part of the package's public API.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "refactor(@angular-devkit/schematics): remove unused code and exports" (#34648)

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/cli): validate dist-tags and manifest caching under modern yarn
Issues.Body:
Modern yarn (`yarn npm info`) silently falls back to the `latest` version with exit code 0 not
only when a requested SemVer version or range is unmet, but also when a requested dist-tag does
not exist. Previously, `getRegistryManifest` only checked valid SemVer ranges, allowing unknown
dist-tags to resolve to `latest`.

Include `dist-tags` in modern yarn's requested `--fields` and add `parseYarnModernManifest` to
verify that non-range version specifiers exist in `dist-tags` and resolve to the returned
manifest version before stripping `dist-tags` from the result.

Move the SemVer range validation inside `#fetchAndParse`'s parser callback so rejected fallback
manifests are cached directly as `null` rather than storing the mismatched manifest object, and
scope `includePrerelease` to wildcard (`*`) specifiers so unmet major or x-ranges do not accept
prerelease `latest` fallbacks.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(@angular/cli): validate dist-tags and manifest caching under modern yarn" (#34637)

Issues.Title: refactor(@angular/build): remove unused exports
Issues.Body: Remove the `export` keyword from four symbols that are only referenced within their defining file: `calculateThresholds` and `checkThresholds`, whose external callers moved to `checkBudgets` in 4d27c38cd4; `augmentAppWithServiceWorkerCore`, which is only called by the exported wrapper functions; and `getEntryPointName`, whose external call sites were removed in 75abe2cc52. The two threshold functions also leave the unsupported `private` entry point, which re-exports the bundle calculator module; neither `@angular-devkit/build-angular` nor `@angular/cli` references them, and both still compile. The public API golden is unchanged.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "refactor(@angular/build): remove unused exports" (#34651)

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/cli): explain the latest version fallback when ng add finds no compatible version
Issues.Body: When no version of the package satisfies the peer dependencies of the project, `ng add` reports `Unable to find compatible package.` and then continues to install the version of the `latest` tag. Issues.Title: fix(material/form-field): support a different direction than the page
Issues.Body:
The form field styles used `[dir='rtl']` selectors, which match any ancestor with `dir="rtl"`. This meant that a form field with `dir="ltr"` inside an RTL page still got the RTL styles: the outline lost its leading border and the label, padding and native select arrow were placed for RTL.

These changes switch the styles to logical properties, so they follow the direction of the form field itself. `transform-origin` and `clip-path` have no logical equivalents, so those two rules use `:dir(rtl)`, which also resolves against the closest element with a `dir` attribute.

Measured in an Angular 22.2 / Material 22.2.6 app (Chromium and Firefox), label offset from the start edge of a `dir="ltr"` field inside a `dir="rtl"` page:

| | Before | After | Plain LTR page |
|---|---|---|---|
| Outline | 29px | 16px | 16px |
| Fill | 65px | 52px | 52px |
| Native select | 33px | 16px | 16px |
| Outline leading border | 0px | 1px | 1px |

Fields in a plain RTL page measure the same before and after.

Fixes #26778.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(material/form-field): support a different direction than the page" (#34081)

Issues.Title: fix(material/list): use theme spacing for leading icons in RTL
Issues.Body:
In RTL, the leading icon of a list item had its margins hardcoded to `32px` and `16px`, instead of using the `leading-icon-start-space` and `leading-icon-end-space` tokens like in LTR. The rule has to use physical properties, because icon font stylesheets (e.g. Material Icons/Symbols) set `direction: ltr` on the icon, which makes the logical margins resolve as LTR inside an RTL list. With the M2 values (16px/32px) this happened to look correct, but with M3 (16px/16px, smaller with density) the gap between the icon and the text was twice as large in RTL.

These changes swap the token values in the RTL rule instead of hardcoding them, so RTL mirrors LTR for any theme.

Measured in an Angular 22.2 / Material 22.2.6 app (Chromium and Firefox), edge → icon / icon → text:

| Tokens | LTR | RTL before | RTL after |
|---|---|---|---|
| M3 default (16/16) | 16 / 16 | 16 / **32** | 16 / 16 |
| M3 density -2 (8/8) | 8 / 8 | **16 / 32** | 8 / 8 |
| M2 (16/32) | 16 / 32 | 16 / 32 | 16 / 32 |

Fixes #30537.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(material/list): use theme spacing for leading icons in RTL" (#34080)

Issues.Title: fix(aria/grid): activate composed widgets when child inputs receive focus
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Fixes #34076.

Focusing a child input inside a complex GridCellWidget composed through hostDirectives leaves the widget in cell mode. Add the static ngGridCellWidget host attribute so GridCell._getWidget() can find the containing widget and forward focus events. This follows the static marker approach used in #33839.

Add two tests comparing standard and composed widgets. Both verify that the input receives real DOM focus and the widget activates. The composed case fails before the fix.

[StackBlitz reproduction](https://stackblitz.com/edit/stackblitz-starters-pbfss5v2?file=src%2Fmain.ts): click each input and compare the displayed CELL/WIDGET mode. Detailed steps are in #34076.

This PR is independent of #34075 and addresses widget activation rather than cell selection.

## Validation

- Chromium grid suite passes with the fix (`pnpm test src/aria/grid --no-watch`).
- `pnpm bazelisk test //goldens:aria_api` passes; no public API changes.
- Targeted TSLint, `pnpm ng-dev format changed --check`, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Confirmed the published-package bug with actual mouse clicks in Chrome using the StackBlitz reproduction (Angular 22.2.4, Aria 22.2.6).

Full repository suites and Firefox were not run locally.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(aria/grid): activate composed widgets when child inputs receive focus" (#34077)

Issues.Title: bug(aria/grid): composed cell widgets do not activate when child inputs receive focus
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

A complex GridCellWidget composed through hostDirectives does not enter widget mode when a child input receives focus. The same markup with ngGridCellWidget applied directly works. Focus reaches the input in both cases; the difference is widget activation.

GridCell._getWidget() searches ancestors using [ngGridCellWidget], but this attribute is absent when the directive is composed. As a result, the focusin event is not forwarded to the widget pattern. This concerns widget activation, separately from cell selection in #34074.

Regression status: unknown.

### Reproduction

[Open the minimal StackBlitz reproduction](https://stackblitz.com/edit/stackblitz-starters-pbfss5v2?file=src%2Fmain.ts).

1. Wait for the preview to display “Grid widget child focus”.
2. Click the input under “Standard directive”. Its Mode changes from CELL to WIDGET.
3. Click the input under “Composed host directive”. The input receives focus, but its Mode stays CELL.
4. Compare the two implementations in src/main.ts: both use widgetType="complex" and contain an input; the second applies GridCellWidget through hostDirectives.

The displayed Mode reads GridCellWidget.isActivated(). No synthetic events are needed.

### Expected Behavior

Both widgets should enter WIDGET mode when their child input receives focus, so grid navigation is suspended while interacting with the widget.

### Actual Behavior

The standard widget activates. The composed widget remains in CELL mode even though its child input is focused.

### Environment

- Angular: 22.2.4
- @angular/aria and @angular/cdk: 22.2.6
- Browser: Chrome
- OS: macOS (Apple Silicon)

Also reproduced in the repository Chromium grid tests: the standard control passes and the composed case fails.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "bug(aria/grid): composed cell widgets do not activate when child inputs receive focus" (#34076)

Issues.Title: fix(aria/grid): select composed cells when clicking child content
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Fixes #34074.

With explicit selection enabled, clicking child content inside a cell composed through `hostDirectives` moves focus but does not select the cell. Clicking the cell host directly works. `Grid._getCell()` searches ancestors using `[ngGridCell]`, but that attribute is absent on composed cells.

Add the static `ngGridCell` host attribute so the existing lookup can find the containing cell. This follows the same approach as #33839 for accordion and adds no signal reads to the grid's host bindings.

Add six regression/control cases covering direct usage, host directives, and inheritance, with clicks on both the host and child content. The tests focus the cell first and verify that the subsequent click changes `aria-selected` from `false` to `true`.

[StackBlitz reproduction](https://stackblitz.com/edit/stackblitz-starters-1z1y55cn?file=src%2Fmain.ts) — blue indicates the active cell; a green outline indicates selection. Detailed mouse-click steps are in #34074.

## Validation

- Before the fix: Chromium grid suite reports **75 passed, 2 failed**, for child clicks on composed and inherited cells.
- After the fix: `pnpm test src/aria/grid --no-watch` passes, **77 specs, 0 failures**.
- `pnpm bazelisk test //goldens:aria_api` passes; no API golden changes.
- TSLint for both changed files, `pnpm ng-dev format changed --check`, and `git diff --check` pass.

Tested locally on macOS arm64 with Node.js 22.23.4 and pnpm 12.16.1. The full repository test suites and Firefox were not run locally.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(aria/grid): select composed cells when clicking child content" (#34075)

Issues.Title: bug(aria/grid): clicking child content does not select cells using hostDirectives
Issues.Body: ### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version ### The previous version in which this bug was not present was _No response_ ### Description When `GridCell` is applied to a reusable component through `hostDirectives`, clicking text inside a child `` moves focus to the cell but does not select it. Clicking the padding on the same cell selects it correctly. The reproduction shows a standard grid and a grid using `hostDirectives` side by side. Both use `enableSelection`, `selectionMode="explicit"`, and `multi`. The standard grid selects cells when clicking either their text or their padding. The reusable cell is defined as follows: ```ts @Component({ selector: 'composed-grid-cell', template: '', hostDirectives: [GridCell], }) class ComposedGridCell {} ``` Its content is ordinary markup, for example `Composed: Second`. This makes the clickable behavior depend on whether the user clicks the text or the surrounding padding. ### Reproduction StackBlitz: https://stackblitz.com/edit/stackblitz-starters-1z1y55cn?file=src%2Fmain.ts Wait for the preview to load. It uses Angular 22.2.4 and @angular/aria 22.2.6. **Visual indicators:** blue background = active/focused cell; green outline = selected cell. The dashed rectangle marks the child ``; the surrounding padding belongs directly to the cell host. Steps to reproduce with actual mouse clicks: 1. In the first grid, under **Direct ngGridCell**, click the text **Standard: Second** inside the dashed rectangle. The cell turns blue and gets a green outline: it is active and selected. 2. In the second grid, under **hostDirectives**, click the text **Composed: Second** inside the dashed rectangle. The cell turns blue but gets **no green outline**: focus moves, but selection does not change. 3. Click the padding of that same **Composed: Second** cell, outside its dashed rectangle. A green outline now appears: clicking the host directly selects it. Reload the preview to reset the demonstration. ### Expected Behavior With selection enabled, clicking non-interactive child content inside a cell should select the containing cell, just as clicking the cell host does. Using `GridCell` through `hostDirectives` should behave like direct `ngGridCell` usage. ### Actual Behavior | Usage / click target | Focus moves to second cell | Second cell selected | | --- | --- | --- | | Direct `ngGridCell`: child text | Yes | Yes | | `hostDirectives`: child text | Yes | **No** | | `hostDirectives`: cell padding | Yes | Yes | After clicking **Composed: Second** text, its host has `data-active="true"` but `aria-selected="false"`. Clicking its padding changes `aria-selected` to `"true"`. Possible cause: `Grid._getCell()` searches ancestors with `closest('[ngGridCell]')`, but `GridCell` does not declare that marker as a static host attribute. The marker is present with direct template usage and absent with `hostDirectives`. This report is limited to the cell selection behavior demonstrated above. It does not claim that focus fails to move, or that `GridCellWidget` is affected. ### Environment - Angular: 22.2.4 - Angular CLI / build: 22.2.4 - @angular/aria: 22.2.6 - @angular/cdk: 22.2.6 - TypeScript: 6.0.3 - Browser: Google Chrome - Operating system: macOS (Apple silicon) - Reproduction runs in StackBlitz. Regression status: unknown; an earlier working version has not been identified.

Issues.Title: feat(aria/menu): expose the trigger's tabindex as a public signal on MenuTrigger
Issues.Body:
### Feature Description

`MenuTrigger` computes its own tabindex (`0`, or `-1` while its open menu holds the active item) and binds it to the host (`'[attr.tabindex]': '_pattern.tabIndex()'`), but the value is only reachable through the underscored `_pattern`:
https://github.com/angular/components/blob/5856d87e9ebd802c6e608b9079f220ea9d5b84d1/src/aria/menu/menu-trigger.ts#L45

`Menu` already exposes the same thing publicly (`readonly tabIndex = computed(() => this._pattern.tabIndex())`):
https://github.com/angular/components/blob/5856d87e9ebd802c6e608b9079f220ea9d5b84d1/src/aria/menu/menu.ts#L144

The request: add the equivalent `readonly tabIndex` signal to `MenuTrigger`, next to its public `expanded` and `hasPopup`.

### Use Case

A menu trigger inside a roving-tabindex container, such as a keyboard-navigable grid or toolbar not built on `ngToolbar`/`ngGrid`. The container keeps the trigger at `tabindex="-1"` until its cell is active, while the trigger must keep aria's own `-1` while its open menu holds focus. A wrapper directive therefore combines the container's value with the trigger's own, taking the lower of the two.

Today that wrapper has to read `trigger._pattern.tabIndex()`. Deriving it from public state (`expanded() ? -1 : 0`) is wrong while the menu is open but has no active item yet, when aria keeps `0`.

A public `tabIndex` signal would make this composition possible without depending on `_pattern`. An input to let a consumer supply the tabindex would also solve it.

---
_This issue was drafted and filed by Claude Code (an AI coding agent) on behalf of artaommahe._
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "feat(aria/menu): expose the trigger's tabindex as a public signal on MenuTrigger" (#34073)

Issues.Title: bug(aria/menu): Enter on a menu item doesn't activate the element, so link items and (click) handlers are mouse-only
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

Activating a menu item with the keyboard never reaches the item's element:

- `<a ngMenuItem href="...">` (or with `routerLink`) doesn't navigate on Enter.
- A `(click)` handler on `<button ngMenuItem>` doesn't run on Enter.

Clicking either item with the mouse works.

The menu's `KeyboardEventManager` calls `preventDefault()` on handled keys by default (https://github.com/angular/components/blob/5856d87e9ebd802c6e608b9079f220ea9d5b84d1/src/aria/private/behaviors/event-manager/keyboard-event-manager.ts#L34), which cancels the browser's own activation of a link or button. `MenuPattern.submit()` then closes the menu and emits `itemSelected`, but never activates the item itself (https://github.com/angular/components/blob/5856d87e9ebd802c6e608b9079f220ea9d5b84d1/src/aria/private/menu/menu.ts#L404-L421).

Navigation menus are a common use, and the WAI-ARIA APG navigation menubar example is built from `<a role="menuitem" href>` items that Enter follows. With the current behaviour, routing has to be rebuilt by hand in `itemSelected`, which also loses the href behaviours a link gives (open in new tab, etc.).

A possible fix: have `submit()` call `item.element.click()`. That's what native buttons and links do on Enter, and it makes keyboard and pointer activation run the same path.

### Reproduction

StackBlitz link: https://stackblitz.com/github/artaommahe/aria-menu-repro
Repo: https://github.com/artaommahe/aria-menu-repro (section B; `node check.mjs` runs the steps with Playwright)
Steps to reproduce:
1. Tab to "Open menu B" and press Enter. Focus is on "Go to #target" (`<a ngMenuItem href="#target">`).
2. Press Enter.
3. Reopen the menu, ArrowDown to "Button with (click)" and press Enter.
4. For comparison, click both items with the mouse.

### Expected Behavior

Step 2 navigates to #target, and step 3 runs the item's (click) handler ("(click) ran" appears in the log), the same as clicking them with the mouse.

### Actual Behavior

In both steps the menu closes and focus returns to the trigger, but the URL doesn't change and the (click) handler never runs. Mouse clicks navigate and run the handler.

### Environment

- Angular: 22.2.4
- CDK/Material: 22.2.6 (@angular/aria 22.2.6)
- Browser(s): Chromium 156
- Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): macOS

---

Issues.Title: bug(aria/menu): Escape inside a submenu closes the whole menu instead of only the submenu
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

Pressing Escape while focus is in a submenu closes every open menu and moves focus back to the root `ngMenuTrigger`. `MenuPattern` maps Escape to `closeAll()`:
https://github.com/angular/components/blob/5856d87e9ebd802c6e608b9079f220ea9d5b84d1/src/aria/private/menu/menu.ts#L182

The WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices menu pattern specifies one level: "Escape: Close the menu that contains focus and return focus to the element or context, e.g., menu button or parent menuitem, from which the menu was opened." (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menubar/). The APG navigation menubar example behaves that way.

The other Angular menus already do: `@angular/cdk/menu` closes only the current menu and focuses its parent trigger (https://github.com/angular/components/blob/5856d87e9ebd802c6e608b9079f220ea9d5b84d1/src/cdk/menu/menu.ts#L84-L90), and `mat-menu` does the same. So a menu migrated from CDK or Material to `@angular/aria` changes keyboard behaviour.

If closing the whole tree is intended, an option to close one level would help, similar to Base UI's `closeParentOnEsc`.

### Reproduction

StackBlitz link: https://stackblitz.com/github/artaommahe/aria-menu-repro
Repo: https://github.com/artaommahe/aria-menu-repro (section A; `node check.mjs` runs the steps with Playwright)
Steps to reproduce:
1. Tab to "Open menu A" and press Enter.
2. ArrowDown to "Categorize" and press ArrowRight. The submenu opens with focus on "Mark as important".
3. Press Escape.

### Expected Behavior

Only the submenu closes. Focus returns to "Categorize", and the root menu stays open.

### Actual Behavior

Both menus close and focus returns to the "Open menu A" trigger.

### Environment

- Angular: 22.2.4
- CDK/Material: 22.2.6 (@angular/aria 22.2.6)
- Browser(s): Chromium 156
- Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): macOS
