This PR contains the following updates: | Package | Change | [Age](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Adoption](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Passing](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Confidence](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | [pnpm](https://pnpm.io) ([source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/tree/HEAD/pnpm/npm/pnpm)) | [`11.28.6` → `11.28.11`](https://renovatebot.com/diffs/npm/pnpm/11.28.6/11.28.11) | ![age](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/age/npm/pnpm/11.28.11?slim=true) | ![adoption](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/adoption/npm/pnpm/11.28.11?slim=true) | ![passing](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/compatibility/npm/pnpm/11.28.6/11.28.11?slim=true) | ![confidence](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/confidence/npm/pnpm/11.28.6/11.28.11?slim=true) | --- - [ ] If you want to rebase/retry this PR, check this box --- ### Release Notes
pnpm/pnpm (pnpm) ### [`v11.28.11`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v11.28.11): pnpm 11.28.11 [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v11.28.10...v11.28.11) pnpm 11.28.11 fixes frozen installs with `excludeLinksFromLockfile`, `pnpm link` in workspaces, `pnpm deploy` with dangling symlinks, and `verifyDepsBeforeRun` starting needless installs. ##### Patch Changes ##### Installing packages - `pnpm deploy` now keeps a symlink in the project whose target is missing from the source, such as a link into a `node_modules` directory that was removed after the build. Deploy used to fail with `ENOENT` on such a link [#​17571](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17571). - A package with `bundledDependencies` and a build script now keeps its bundled dependencies when it is restored from the side-effects cache [#​17523](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17523). - `pnpm install` now links the runtime that an earlier `pnpm install --no-runtime` skipped [#​17542](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17542). - Commands of a package whose `bin` paths contain excess parent directory segments, such as `../dist/cli.js`, are no longer missing. Such paths now resolve inside the package [#​17586](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17586). - Generated POSIX shell shims now quote their paths, so shell special characters in a path stay literal. - A repeat `pnpm install` now rewrites the bin shims after `extendNodePath` changes. Before, it reported "Already up to date" and the shims kept the `NODE_PATH` of the previous setting. ##### Lockfile and resolution - `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` now accepts the lockfile it wrote with `excludeLinksFromLockfile` and `linkWorkspacePackages` on, when a project depends on a workspace package through a plain version range or a `catalog:` entry. It used to fail with `ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE`. - `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm approve-builds`, and `pnpm rebuild` now accept a lockfile that resolves a `*` dependency to a prerelease `latest` version. pnpm wrote such a lockfile and then reported it as outdated [#​17594](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17594). - Packages from the default registry keep plain lockfile keys, even when a prefix such as `npmjs` points at the registry set as `registry`. A dependency written with such a prefix shares the plain entry of the same package. The next install rewrites keys that earlier versions qualified this way [#​17575](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17575). - Relative local paths in root `overrides` now resolve from the workspace root when each project has its own lockfile [#​17691](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17691). Installing a local directory dependency no longer fails when another project's install is writing a lockfile in that directory. - Peer deduplication no longer gives a project different copies of a dependency across direct and transitive paths when an optional peer has no provider [#​17666](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17666). - A Node.js version range such as `>=26.13`, for example in `devEngines.runtime`, now resolves to the newest stable release that satisfies it. pnpm picks a prerelease only when no stable release matches [#​17516](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17516). ##### verifyDepsBeforeRun - With `verifyDepsBeforeRun`, `pnpm run` and `pnpm exec` now report dependencies as out of date after a dependency is added to the `package.json` of a local directory dependency, such as `"lib": "file:../lib"`. Before, the command ran without the new dependency installed. - `verifyDepsBeforeRun` no longer reports dependencies as out of sync when only the `version` field of a single-project repository changed [#​17560](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17560). The same holds for a workspace project that no dependency can resolve to. A script run after such a change no longer starts an install first. ##### pnpm link - In a workspace, `pnpm link ` now adds the `link:` dependency to the `package.json` of the project where the command runs, not to the workspace root's `package.json`. The link is created in that project's `node_modules`, as documented. The override is still written to the root `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. - `pnpm link` with several paths now records every linked package in the `overrides` of `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. Some of them could be missing before. - `pnpm link` now fails without changing `package.json` or `pnpm-workspace.yaml` when the linked package's name is not a valid npm package name. It used to write that name to both files, which made every later install fail [#​17475](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17475). ##### pnpm update - `pnpm update` with only negated selectors, such as `pnpm update '!foo'`, now leaves the dependencies listed in `update.ignoreDeps` unchanged [pnpm/tasks#243](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/243). - `pnpm update --depth 0` without selectors now does nothing when every direct dependency is listed in `update.ignoreDeps`. Before, it failed with `ERR_PNPM_NO_PACKAGE_IN_DEPENDENCIES` [pnpm/tasks#251](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/251). ##### Store and self-update - `pnpm store prune` now keeps packages linked from a configured modules directory [pnpm/tasks#230](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/230). - `pnpm store status` no longer reports untouched packages as modified when the global virtual store is enabled. If the installed global-store layout cannot be verified, the command reports `ERR_PNPM_STORE_STATUS_UNVERIFIABLE` and asks for a reinstall [#​17631](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17631). - `pnpm store add` now fails right away with `ERR_PNPM_FROZEN_STORE_WRITE` when `frozenStore` is enabled. It used to retry each download for minutes before failing, or fail with a SQLite error on an empty store. - `pnpm self-update` now reinstalls a cached engine if its executable cannot run. This repairs shared store entries damaged by an earlier install [#​17582](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17582). #### Platinum Sponsors
#### Gold Sponsors
### [`v11.28.10`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v11.28.10): pnpm 11.28.10 [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v11.28.9...v11.28.10) pnpm 11.28.10 stops `pnpm store prune` from deleting other stores when `cacheDir` points to their parent directory. It also fixes globally installed commands that load hoisted dependencies, and repeat installs that missed changes to local dependencies. ##### Patch Changes ##### Installing packages - `pnpm store prune` preserves other stores and global package data when `cacheDir` points to their parent directory. - Commands installed with `pnpm add --global` now find the dependencies that pnpm hoists for their package. A package that loads a dependency it does not declare, such as a native addon's platform-specific package, failed with "Cannot find module". Reinstall such a package with `pnpm add --global` to update its existing command [#​17503](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17503). - `pnpm prune --prod` no longer fails with `ERR_PNPM_EXDEV` when `node_modules` was copied from an earlier Docker build stage [#​17424](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17424). - `pnpm install` now retries a Node.js runtime zip download when the connection drops partway through. A download that still fails names its URL. Before, a single dropped connection ended the install with `terminated` [#​17411](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17411). - With the global virtual store, a change to a dependency of one package in a dependency cycle now gives every package in that cycle a new directory. Before, the other packages kept their directories and still linked the old copy of the changed package, so the project could load two copies of it [#​17466](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17466). Packages in a dependency cycle, and packages that depend on one, move to new global virtual store directories once after this update. Those that run a build miss the side-effects cache once. - `pnpm install` and `pnpm rebuild` now refresh privately hoisted `.bin` shims in `node_modules/.pnpm/node_modules/.bin` after a dependency build replaces a script target with a native executable [#​17402](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17402). - The Node.js `latest` selector now chooses the newest stable release [#​17490](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17490). - The standalone `@pnpm/exe` builds now embed Node.js 26.13.0. ##### Repeat installs and lockfiles - `pnpm install` now resolves a local directory again after its `package.json` changes when an override or a package extension adds it to the dependencies of a registry package. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` fails on a lockfile that still records the old dependencies of such a directory [#​17486](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17486). - With `injectWorkspacePackages` and per-project lockfiles, `pnpm install` now updates a project's lockfile when a local tarball that an injected workspace project depends on is replaced. The project's lockfile kept the old version and integrity before. - `pnpm install` now detects a change to a local tarball or directory that only a pnpmfile `readPackage` hook depends on. A repeat install reported "Already up to date" and kept the old contents before [pnpm/tasks#227](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/227). - `pnpm install` now relinks a `workspace:` or `link:` dependency whose link was deleted from `node_modules`. It used to report "Already up to date" and leave the link missing [#​17485](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17485). - Merging git branch lockfiles now keeps a workspace project whose directory is named `__proto__`. It was dropped from the merged lockfile before [pnpm/tasks#59](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/59). ##### Adding and publishing packages - `pnpm add` no longer rewrites a catalog entry set to the dist-tag that the dependency resolves through. For example, an entry `beta` stays `beta` after `pnpm add foo@beta` or `pnpm add foo`. Before, the entry was replaced with the version the tag pointed to [pnpm/tasks#225](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/225). - `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` now always include the binary file declared by a string `bin` field in `package.json`, even when `files` or `.npmignore` would otherwise exclude it. - When the version or range given to `pnpm unpublish` matches every published version, the error now says so and shows the same command with `--force`. It suggested running `pnpm unpublish @`, the command that had just failed. ##### Running commands - Every command, including `pnpm --version`, `pnpm self-update`, and invocations with unknown flags, now applies the same `packageManager` and `devEngines.packageManager` settings when switching to the pinned pnpm version or recording it in `pnpm-lock.yaml`. `--config.` flags and `lockfileDir` now reach the version switch and lockfile sync on every entry point. Unreadable settings in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` or the global `config.yaml` that do not affect the pin decision no longer block the version switch [pnpm/tasks#222](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/222). - On Windows, the shell shim of a `.cmd` or `.bat` bin now runs it under Git Bash when MSYS argument conversion is off, such as with `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` or `MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL='*'`. The shim used to start an interactive cmd.exe prompt [#​17480](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17480). - `pnx` and `pnpm create` now run the command in the directory selected by `--dir` or `--workspace-root`. Without either flag, the command still runs in the directory pnpm was started in. - The error for a dependency with an invalid name in a project's manifest now names the project's directory. It used to say only "The current package", which did not tell which workspace project to fix [#​17475](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17475). #### Platinum Sponsors
#### Gold Sponsors
### [`v11.28.9`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v11.28.9): pnpm 11.28.9 [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v11.28.8...v11.28.9) This release fixes a crash on registry responses with too many content encodings ([GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c)) and sizes the install worker pool by the container's CPU quota. A repeat `pnpm install` now acts on more setting changes. ##### Patch Changes ##### Crashes and security - A registry response with too many content encodings can no longer crash pnpm. pnpm now uses undici 7.30.1, which fixes [GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c). - `pnpm install` now sizes its worker pool by the CPU quota of the container it runs in, such as a Kubernetes CPU limit, when that quota is smaller than the number of CPUs the container may run on. The default `workspaceConcurrency` respects the quota the same way. On a CI runner with a 4-CPU quota and hundreds of host CPUs, pnpm started hundreds of workers and ran out of memory [#​17382](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17382). ##### Repeat installs and changed settings - A repeat `pnpm install` now acts on a change to these settings. Before, it reported "Already up to date". - `storeDir` or `virtualStoreDir`: it recreates `node_modules`. - `virtualStoreDirMaxLength`: it renames the virtual store directories. - `dangerouslyAllowAllBuilds` turned on: it runs the builds it skipped. - `trustLockfile` turned off: it verifies the lockfile. - `pnpm add`, `pnpm remove`, and `pnpm update` now fail when the `node-linker` setting differs from the one recorded in `node_modules`. A `pnpm install` of the whole workspace recreates `node_modules` with the new `node-linker`, and an install filtered to some projects fails [pnpm/tasks#203](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/203). - An install filtered to some workspace projects now fails if `node_modules` was installed with a different `nodeLinker`, `hoistPattern`, `publicHoistPattern`, store, or virtual store. Before, it recreated `node_modules` and left the projects it skipped without their dependencies. A `pnpm install` of the whole workspace still recreates `node_modules` [pnpm/tasks#217](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/217). - `pnpm install` now takes its fast path in a workspace with `patchedDependencies` when the previous install ran with another major version of pnpm. - `pnpm install` now relinks the bins of a workspace package when its `bin` field changes, including with `--frozen-lockfile` and an unchanged lockfile. A filtered install relinks them in the selected projects, and the next install that covers the remaining projects relinks them there [#​17324](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17324). - `pnpm install` now removes command shims from `node_modules/.bin` when a workspace dependency renames or removes an entry from its `bin` field [pnpm/tasks#211](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/211). - With `nodeLinker: hoisted`, an install that stops partway no longer leaves the next install trusting the packages it was replacing. Before, reverting the change that started the stopped install, such as a patch edit, kept the half-replaced package in `node_modules`. - `pnpm run` and `pnpm exec` no longer report the dependencies as out of date after a lockfile change when `dedupePeers` is `true` [#​17322](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17322). ##### Resolving dependencies and the lockfile - A package that a plain range and a `:` specifier both resolve from one registry is now recorded once in `pnpm-lock.yaml` and installed once. The lockfile key names the registry a package resolved from. When that registry declares a prefix, through `prefix` in `registries` or through `namedRegistries`, the package is keyed `@:` however its dependency was written: with the prefix, as a plain range its scope routes to that registry, or through the default registry. Before, the plain range was keyed `@`, so one tarball was installed twice and `instanceof` checks and module singletons broke between the two copies. The same name and version served by two registries still get separate entries. When several prefixes declare one registry, its packages are keyed by the lexicographically smallest prefix. If a scope you route reaches a registry that also declares a prefix, your next `pnpm install` re-keys those entries, which shows up as a lockfile diff. Commit it. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` installs the lockfile as recorded. - `pnpm install` now resolves a scope's packages again when the scope is routed to another registry in `registries`. Before, the lockfile kept the versions and integrity resolved from the old registry, so the install failed when the new registry did not serve a locked version or served different content. pnpm records in the workspace state which registry each scope routed to, so a fresh clone without that record installs the lockfile as recorded. Changing the default registry resolves nothing again, and `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` is unchanged. - An optional dependency written with a named-registry prefix, such as `work:^1.0.0`, now fails the install when it cannot be resolved but the lockfile already has a matching entry from that registry. Such a dependency was skipped, which removed its entries from the lockfile. - With `injectWorkspacePackages: true`, a `workspace:` dependency written as a relative path, such as `workspace:../lib-a`, in a workspace package now resolves from that package's directory [#​17284](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17284). - Fixed `pnpm install` failing with `ERR_PNPM_UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL` when a workspace package injected through a relative path, such as `workspace:../lib`, has `catalog:` dependencies. Their catalog entries now resolve the way they do for a package injected by name [#​17280](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17280). - `pnpm install` now applies the `serverType` registry setting when it updates the lockfile for an override or catalog change without a full resolution. pnpm wrote the tarball URLs of a declared registry into the lockfile in that case. - Added the `pnpr` value to the `serverType` registry setting. pnpm leaves the tarball URLs of a pnpr registry out of `pnpm-lock.yaml`. - A `registries` entry whose `prefix` is `__proto__` is no longer ignored. - Installs delegated to a pnpr server now resolve every prefix declared for a registry URL. A dependency or lockfile entry that used the second of two prefixes for the same registry, such as `zeta:` next to `work:` in `namedRegistries`, failed on the server [pnpm/tasks#204](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/204). ##### Registries, proxies, and downloading pnpm - The proxy settings `httpProxy`, `httpsProxy`, `noProxy`, `proxy`, and `noproxy` set in the global `config.yaml`, through `PNPM_CONFIG_HTTPS_PROXY` and the matching variables, or as `--config.httpsProxy` on the command line now apply to `pnpm self-update` and to the download of the pnpm version pinned in `packageManager`. Previously, these requests read the proxy only from `.npmrc` and the `HTTPS_PROXY` family of variables [pnpm/tasks#215](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/215). - When `https-proxy` is `false`, pnpm now downloads the pnpm version pinned by `packageManager` through the legacy `proxy` setting, as installs already do. Setting `proxy` to `false` now also stops that download from using the `HTTP_PROXY` environment variable. The signature check of the pinned pnpm now uses the same proxy and TLS settings as its download [pnpm/tasks#193](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/193). - `strictSsl` and `localAddress` set in the global `config.yaml`, through `PNPM_CONFIG_STRICT_SSL` and `PNPM_CONFIG_LOCAL_ADDRESS`, or on the command line now apply to `pnpm self-update` and to the download of the pnpm version pinned in `packageManager`. These requests read them from `.npmrc` only before. `--config.localAddress` now reaches them in the camelCase spelling too [pnpm/tasks#201](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/201). ##### Commands - `pnpm audit --ignore` and `pnpm audit --ignore-unfixable` now exit with a non-zero code when vulnerabilities at or above the audit level remain after ignoring. Before, these commands always exited with code 0. - `pnpm audit --fix` and `pnpm audit --interactive` now fail with `ERR_PNPM_AUDIT_FIX_WITH_IGNORE` when combined with `--ignore` or `--ignore-unfixable`. Before, the fix ran and the ignore flags had no effect. - `pnpm ci --lockfile` and `pnpm ci --config.lockfile=true` no longer delete `pnpm-lock.yaml`. `pnpm ci` now always keeps the lockfile and runs a frozen install from it. - `pnpm deploy` now keeps a deployed symlink to a directory inside the project even if the directory is not among the deployed files, such as a link into `node_modules` [#​17288](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17288). - `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` again include the files of a `publishConfig.directory` that is reached through a symlink, together with its bundled dependencies [#​17390](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17390). - `pnpm -r publish --batch` now sends `PUT /-/pnpr/v0/publish`, the batch publish endpoint that pnpr serves. - `pnpm store prune` now keeps the packages that a project still uses when pnpm copied or cloned them into `node_modules`. These include patched packages, built packages, and every package installed with `packageImportMethod: copy`. Before, the prune removed them, and the next install downloaded them again [#​7192](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/7192). - `pnpm store prune` now keeps the packages of a project that was installed with a different symlinked spelling of the store path. Previously, prune dropped such a project from its list and removed the packages only that project used from the global virtual store. ##### Speed and output - Sped up installs of projects whose local directory dependencies share transitive local directory dependencies. pnpm no longer checks a shared directory again for each direct dependency that reaches it [#​17374](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17374). - Output that fills the terminal, such as `pnpm run --stream` script output, is now written once. Before, every new line also rewrote all the lines already on screen [#​17387](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17387). - The warning about unrecognized settings now marks `symlinkedLockfileTargetDirs` as a setting of a newer pnpm version. #### Platinum Sponsors

### [`v11.28.8`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v11.28.8): pnpm 11.28.8 [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v11.28.7...v11.28.8) ##### Patch Changes - The standalone `@pnpm/exe` builds now embed Node.js 26.12.1. --- ### Configuration and setting up pnpm - pnpm now recognizes `externalDependencies` and `autoInstallPeersFromHighestMatch` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` without warning and forwards both settings to `pnpm install`. Previously, setting `externalDependencies` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` with `nodeLinker: hoisted` crashed `pnpm install` with `externalDependencies.has is not a function` [pnpm/tasks#166](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/166). - pnpm now ignores a `PNPM_CONFIG_*` environment variable for a URL setting, such as `PNPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY`, when its value is not a URL. Such a value used to make every command fail with `Invalid URL`. - The warning about unrecognized settings in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` and the global `config.yaml` now names `addMissingPeerTypes`, `autoDedupe`, `bootConfig`, `macosBackup`, `nodePackageMap`, `permissions`, `pipelineBase`, `publishWaitTimeout`, `python`, `remoteCache`, `saveTypes`, `skills`, `storeIndexFormat`, and `tools` as pnpm v12 settings [pnpm/tasks#167](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/167). - When a config file has a setting pnpm cannot read, `pnpm --version` now prints the version, and `pmOnFail` and `lockfileDir` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` stay in force. Previously, pnpm switched to the pinned version despite `pmOnFail: ignore`. pnpm also no longer writes the pinned version to `pnpm-lock.yaml` when it cannot read every setting and the running pnpm already matches the pin. - pnpm now records the pinned pnpm version in the `pnpm-lock.yaml` under the `lockfileDir` set in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, and resolves a relative `lockfileDir` from the workspace root. pnpm used to write a second `pnpm-lock.yaml` at the workspace root. - `pnpm self-update` now updates the project's pnpm pin when Homebrew installed pnpm or Corepack runs it. The global pnpm is left alone [#​17001](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17001). - `pnpm setup` now completes when Windows registry environment values cannot be read or written. It prints PowerShell commands to configure `PNPM_HOME` and `PATH` without registry access [#​17167](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17167). - `pnpm setup` now succeeds when it cannot tell which shell configuration file to update, for example in a container where `SHELL` is not set. It installs pnpm and prints the `PNPM_HOME` and `PATH` lines to add yourself. Previously it failed with `ERR_PNPM_UNKNOWN_SHELL`, and so did the installer script at get.pnpm.io [#​16973](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16973). #### Platinum Sponsors

### [`v12.18.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.18.0): pnpm 12.18

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.17.0...v12.18.0)

pnpm 12.18.0 packs, publishes, and installs packages with platform variants on pnpr registries. It also adds per-skill approval of agent skills and `pnpm store add` for offline installs from downloaded tarballs. Repeat installs and `verifyDepsBeforeRun` no longer read the `package.json` of unchanged workspace projects. The release fixes several peer dependency resolution bugs too.

##### Minor Changes

##### Agent skills

- pnpm now names the link to a dependency's agent skill after the skill alone. A skill that the `@acme/kit` package ships in `skills/auth/` is linked as `.claude/skills/auth`, not `.claude/skills/pnpm-@acme+kit-auth`. The next install replaces links with the old names. pnpm lists the linked skills in a `# pnpm` block of each agent skill directory's `.gitignore` [#​17455](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/discussions/17455).

  When two approved packages ship a skill of the same name, or the name is already taken in an agent skill directory, pnpm links the skill as `pnpm-<package>-<skill>`. Before, the install failed.

- `pnpm approve` now asks which agent skills to link when a package ships more than one. pnpm records the chosen skills as a list, such as `permissions.<pkg>.skills: [guide, migrate]`, and does not offer the other skills for approval again. The first time a project approves a skill, `pnpm approve` also asks which agent directories to link skills into, and records the answer under `skills.dirs`.

- pnpm links agent skills nested in category directories, such as `skills/engineering/implement/SKILL.md`, up to three levels below `skills/`. Before, it linked only the skills directly under `skills/`.

##### Platform variants

These features need a registry declared with `serverType: pnpr`.

- `pnpm pack` packs one archive per entry of `publishConfig.variants`, each platform variant as `<name>-<version>~<tag>.tgz`. `pnpm pack --variant <target>` packs only the archive whose entry lists that target. `pnpm pack --json` prints the `integrity` and `size` of every archive it writes.

- `pnpm publish` publishes a package's `publishConfig.variants`. pnpm uploads every archive before the publish request that references them. Publishing variants to any other registry is refused unless `--no-variants` is given, which publishes only the archive that targets `any`.

- `pnpm publish --upload-variant <target>` uploads the archive of one `publishConfig.variants` entry to the registry's staging area and prints `<target>=<integrity>`. `pnpm publish --variant-integrity <target>=<integrity>` then publishes the version from archives that other jobs uploaded. With `--recursive`, each value names its package as `<name>~<target>=<integrity>`.

- `pnpm publish -r --batch` now uploads each package archive on its own request and skips archives the registry already holds, so the batch request no longer grows with the archives it publishes. A batch of more than 256 packages still carries every archive inline. Packages with `publishConfig.variants` can be published in a batch. A batch with variants that would reference more than 256 archives on one registry fails with `ERR_PNPM_BATCH_PUBLISH_TOO_MANY_ARCHIVES` [pnpm/tasks#244](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/244).

- `pnpm publish --provenance` signs one statement that names every archive of a version with `publishConfig.variants`. A platform variant's archive is named by the version's package URL with a `variant` qualifier.

- Rerunning `pnpm publish` after the version was already published now succeeds when the published version is the same release. pnpm compares the archives, the provenance statement when the rerun signs one, and the dist-tag. When the published version differs, the publish fails with `ERR_PNPM_PUBLISHED_RELEASE_DIFFERS`, which names what differs.

- pnpm installs the platform variant of a package that fits the host, or the package's own archive when none does. The lockfile records every variant. A version published with variants only, and no archive for other hosts, installs on a host one of the variants fits. On any other host, an optional dependency is skipped, and any other dependency fails with an error that lists the platforms the version is published for.

- `supportedArchitectures` platform lists accept platform tags, the same tags `publishConfig.variants` entries name. An entry can state floors and an ABI, such as `linux-x64-manylinux_2_28`, `darwin-arm64-macos_14_0`, `linux-x64-napi8` or `linux-x64-node127`, and any Node.js OS and CPU, such as `freebsd-x64`. The spellings accepted before still work.

- With `supportedArchitectures` set, pnpm also fetches into the store the variants that the other listed platforms need, when it downloads a package with platform variants.

##### pnpr registries

- pnpm downloads less metadata from a registry declared with `serverType: pnpr`. A large package document leaves out the manifests of rarely picked versions, and pnpm fetches one only when it picks that version. In a benchmark that resolves 787 packages, the package documents shrank from 30.3 MB to 2.5 MB gzipped. pnpm caches these documents in `v12/metadata-pnpr`, and the `pnpm cache` commands cover them.

  pnpm warns when a registry that is not declared `serverType: pnpr` turns out to be pnpr. For a registry declared `serverType: pnpr`, a `minimumReleaseAge` longer than 30 days fails with `ERR_PNPM_UNSUPPORTED_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE`.

- `pnpm publish` sends release notes to registries declared with `serverType: pnpr`. A package's notes are the section for its version in `CHANGELOG.md`, or the notes that `pnpm version -r` composed from change intents. `--release-notes <file>` gives the notes from a file, and `--no-release-notes` sends none. `--publication-name` names a release published with `--batch`.

  In a workspace that uses pnpm's versioning, `pnpm version -r --release-notes <file>` puts a summary above the composed notes of the release.

  `pnpm view <pkg>@<version> releaseNotes`, `pnpm outdated --notes`, and `pnpm update --interactive` show the release notes from these registries.

##### Store and hooks

- `pnpm store add` now prepares the store for offline installs from package tarballs downloaded some other way. After `pnpm store add ./tarballs/*.tgz`, `pnpm install --offline --frozen-lockfile` installs each registry package whose lockfile entry pins one of those tarballs [#​2978](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/2978).

- Custom pnpmfile fetchers can use `fetchers.gitHostedTarball`, `fetchers.git`, and `fetchers.binary` [pnpm/tasks#191](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/191).

##### Patch Changes

##### Installing packages

- Running `node` or `pnpm install` in a project that pins a Node.js version pnpm has not downloaded yet no longer hangs when a `globalPnpmfile` is configured [#​17530](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17530).

- `pnpm install` with `enableGlobalVirtualStore` no longer fails on Windows for a dependency from a named registry, such as `gh:` or `npmjs:` [#​17665](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17665).

- Concurrent installs that share a global virtual store no longer fail with `ERR_PNPM_CMD_SHIM_SYMLINK_BIN` when they link the same executable at the same time [#​17587](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17587).

- `pnpm install` and `pnpm ci` now succeed when dependency skills are approved but no agent skill directory exists. The skills stay unlinked until a directory exists [#​17574](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17574).

- Commands run from a workspace package now use the same default store as the workspace root. Before, `pnpm add` in a package could fail with `ERR_PNPM_UNEXPECTED_STORE` when the workspace root was its own mount point and the home store was on another volume, as in a sandbox or a container.

  A workspace installed with the old behavior may need one `pnpm install --force` from the workspace root.

- `pnpm deploy` now keeps a symlink in the project whose target is missing from the source, such as a link into a `node_modules` directory that was removed after the build. Deploy used to drop such a link silently [#​17571](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17571).

- `pnpm install` now links the runtime that an earlier `pnpm install --no-runtime` skipped, and `pnpm install --no-runtime` removes a runtime that an earlier install linked [#​17542](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17542).

- With `enableGlobalVirtualStore`, `pnpm install` again runs a dependency's build scripts in a project whose global virtual store slot another project already built, unless the side-effects cache has build output to restore for it. A build that writes only outside its own package, such as a git hook installer, now takes effect in every project [#​17526](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17526).

- Commands of a package whose `bin` paths contain excess parent directory segments, such as `../dist/cli.js`, are no longer missing. Such paths now resolve inside the package [#​17586](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17586).

- Generated POSIX shell shims now quote their paths, so shell special characters in a path stay literal.

##### Lockfile and local paths

- Packages from the default registry keep plain lockfile keys, even when a prefix such as `npmjs` points at the registry set as `registry`. A dependency written with such a prefix shares the plain entry of the same package. The next install rewrites keys that earlier versions qualified this way [#​17575](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17575).

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm approve-builds`, and `pnpm rebuild` now accept a lockfile that resolves a `*` dependency to a prerelease `latest` version. pnpm wrote such a lockfile and then reported it as outdated [#​17594](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17594).

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` now accepts a lockfile written with `excludeLinksFromLockfile` and `linkWorkspacePackages` on, when a project depends on a workspace package through a `catalog:` entry. It used to fail with `ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE`.

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` no longer rejects a freshly generated lockfile when `addMissingPeerTypes` is enabled and an injected workspace package has peer dependencies [#​17668](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17668).

- Relative local paths in root `overrides` now resolve from the workspace root when each project has its own lockfile [#​17691](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17691).

  Installing a local directory dependency no longer fails when another project's install is writing a lockfile in that directory.

- Relative local paths in root catalogs now resolve for dependencies and peers [#​17690](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17690).

- `pnpm install` now resolves auto-installed relative `workspace:` and `file:` peers from the directory of the package that declares them [#​17676](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17676), [#​17689](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17689).

- `pnpm dedupe --check` leaves `pnpm-lock.yaml` untouched while it looks for deduplication changes. If `configDependencies` changed since the last install, the check keeps the lockfile they sync, as `pnpm install` does [#​17628](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17628).

- `pnpm dedupe --check` no longer fails when the only difference is the integrity of a locked version that the registry now reports with a stronger algorithm, such as a `sha512` integrity replacing the `sha1` shasum it reported when the lockfile was written [#​17692](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17692).

##### Peer dependencies

- Peer deduplication no longer gives a project different copies of a dependency across direct and transitive paths when an optional peer has no provider [#​17666](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17666).

- Dependencies no longer bind to another project's peer variant when the provider has nested peers, including providers that finish resolving later [#​17593](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17593).

- Re-resolving a lockfile no longer preserves optional peer bindings from other projects when no provider is in scope [#​17592](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17592).

- `pnpm peers check` warns when a required peer is resolved without a provider declared by the project or its dependency ancestors, with `autoInstallPeers: false` and `dedupePeerDependents: true`. These warnings do not change the command's exit code or cause `strictPeerDependencies` failures.

##### Speed and memory

- `pnpm install`, and `pnpm run` and `pnpm exec` with `verifyDepsBeforeRun`, no longer read the `package.json` of workspace projects whose files did not change since the last install. This also holds with a pnpmfile, `configDependencies`, or `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false`. In an up-to-date workspace with `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false`, `pnpm install` no longer runs the install of each project [pnpm/tasks#256](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/256).

- A recursive `pnpm run` or `pnpm exec` with `verifyDepsBeforeRun` set no longer reads every `package.json` in the workspace once per project when `sharedWorkspaceLockfile` is `false`. In a 300-project workspace, `pnpm -r exec true` went from 490 ms to 42 ms [pnpm/tasks#256](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/256).

- `pnpm install` makes fewer `stat` calls when it hardlinks files from the store, as few as 12.7.0 made [#​17543](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17543).

- Picking versions from registry metadata uses less temporary memory.

##### verifyDepsBeforeRun and repeat installs

- With `verifyDepsBeforeRun`, `pnpm run` and `pnpm exec` now report dependencies as out of date after a dependency is added to the `package.json` of a local directory dependency, such as `"lib": "file:../lib"`. Before, the command ran without the new dependency installed.

- `verifyDepsBeforeRun` no longer reports a `file:` directory dependency as out of date after an edit to `package.json` that leaves its dependencies unchanged [#​17697](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17697).

- `verifyDepsBeforeRun` no longer reports dependencies as out of sync when only the `version` field of a single-project repository changed [#​17560](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17560). The same holds for a workspace project that no dependency can resolve to. A script run after such a change no longer starts an install first.

- A repeat `pnpm install` now rewrites the bin shims after `extendNodePath` changes. Before, it reported "Already up to date" and the shims kept the `NODE_PATH` of the previous setting.

##### Adding and updating dependencies

- `pnpm add <pkg>` without a version now saves the range that the other workspace projects declare for the package, or the one a matching override sets. A `catalog:` reference still comes first, and the `tag` setting is used only when none of these exists [pnpm/tasks#191](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/191).

- `pnpm update` with only negated selectors, such as `pnpm update '!foo'`, now leaves the dependencies listed in `update.ignoreDeps` unchanged. Negated `crate:` and `pypi:` selectors, such as `!crate:sha2`, now exclude that dependency and update the rest [pnpm/tasks#243](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/243).

- `pnpm update --latest` keeps three kinds of Cargo dependencies where they are, unless the crate is named on the command line. Before, it moved each one to the newest release and left a workspace that did not build.

  - A renamed dependency, such as `tower-0-4 = { package = "tower", version = "0.4" }`, stays within its requirement if the workspace also declares the crate under its own name.
  - A crate replaced through `[patch.crates-io]` keeps its version, with a warning.
  - A crate whose newest release is older than its current version, such as a prerelease newer than the latest stable release, keeps its version, with a warning. Only an explicit version, such as `pnpm update crate:foo@1`, moves it back.

  Other new major versions are still selected and may need code changes.

- `pnpm update` now keeps a Cargo dependency at its current version, with a warning, if the new version lacks a feature the workspace enables on it. If the crate is named on the command line, as in `pnpm update --latest crate:sha2`, the update fails with an error that names the missing features.

- `pnpm update` now keeps the operator of every existing Cargo requirement, so `~1.0.0` is updated to `~1.1.0`, and an exact `=` requirement stays exact unless the selector gives a range, such as `crate:foo@^2`. The `savePrefix` and `saveExact` settings apply only to new Cargo dependencies. Saved Cargo requirements omit build metadata.

- `pnpm update` now updates a Cargo dependency whose inline table spans several lines, such as one with a multi-line `features` array. It failed with "its Cargo.toml dependency declaration is not a string or single-line inline table".

- `pnpm update` no longer applies the `savePrefix` and `saveExact` settings to Python requirements. A `savePrefix` such as `^` made `pnpm update` fail in a project with Python dependencies.

  `pnpm update` now keeps the precision of a `~=` requirement, so `~=1.0` is updated to `~=1.5` and still allows any 1.x release. With `--latest`, a `==1.*` requirement is updated to `==2.*`.

##### Store

- `pnpm store prune` now keeps packages linked from a configured modules directory [pnpm/tasks#230](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/230).

- `pnpm store prune` now removes aliases of pruned packages.

- `pnpm store status` no longer reports untouched packages as modified when the global virtual store is enabled. If the installed global-store layout cannot be verified, the command reports `ERR_PNPM_STORE_STATUS_UNVERIFIABLE` and asks for a reinstall [#​17631](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17631).

- `pnpm store add` now fails with `ERR_PNPM_FROZEN_STORE_WRITE` when `frozenStore` is enabled. It used to write package files into the read-only store without recording them, so no install could use them.

- `pnpm cat-index <name>@<version>` no longer shows the index of a package whose name differs only in letter case.

##### Other commands and settings

- `pnpm link` now fails without changing `package.json` or `pnpm-workspace.yaml` when the linked package's name is not a valid npm package name. It used to write that name to both files, which made every later install fail [#​17475](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17475).

- `pnpm link <dir>` now resolves a relative `<dir>` against the current directory. In a directory without a `package.json`, such as a workspace's `packages` folder, `pnpm link .` used to link the nearest project above it into itself [#​17475](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17475).

- A Node.js version range such as `>=26.13`, for example in `devEngines.runtime`, now resolves to the newest stable release that satisfies it. pnpm picks a prerelease only when no stable release matches [#​17516](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17516).

- Switching to the pnpm version a project pins no longer writes a temporary `_tmp_*` file into the project directory, which file watchers reported on every command [#​17681](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17681).

- pnpm now reads the `linkWorkspacePackages`, `injectWorkspacePackages`, `extendNodePath`, `frozenStore`, and `optimisticRepeatInstall` settings from `PNPM_CONFIG_*` environment variables, such as `PNPM_CONFIG_LINK_WORKSPACE_PACKAGES=true`. `--config.extend-node-path` now applies too.

- Recursive scripts run with `--sequential` or `--workspace-concurrency=1` print GitHub Actions log groups again [#​17629](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17629).

- When `pnpm docs` cannot open a browser, the URL it prints no longer includes the query string or the fragment.

### [`v12.17.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.17.0): pnpm 12.17

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.16.1...v12.17.0)

pnpm 12.17.0 adds `pnpm peers check --global`, dependency-group selectors and wildcards in `overrides`, and runtime, package manager, Cargo, and Python updates in `pnpm outdated` and `pnpm update`. It also fixes files that other users could not read in Docker images, and repeat installs that missed changes to local dependencies.

##### Minor Changes

- `pnpm peers check` now accepts `--global` (`-g`) to check globally installed packages. After a global install or update, the peer dependency warning now suggests `pnpm peers check -g` [#​17504](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17504).

- `pnpm outdated` and `pnpm update` now inspect and update package manager and runtime versions in `devEngines.packageManager`, `packageManager`, `devEngines.runtime`, `engines.runtime`, and `runtime:` dependencies. With `cargo.enabled` or `python.enabled`, `pnpm outdated` and `pnpm update` also inspect and update Cargo dependencies in `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock` and Python dependencies in `pyproject.toml` and `pylock.toml`.

- `overrides` selectors now support `:prod`, `:optional`, and `:peer` pseudo-selectors that target a single dependency group. They also support `*` wildcard patterns on parent and target package names. An override with a non-range value, such as `npm:` or `file:`, no longer adds a peer dependency to `dependencies`. Removing an optional dependency with `"-"` now also removes the duplicate entry from `dependencies` [#​5391](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/5391).

##### Patch Changes

##### Installing packages

- Files that pnpm creates in a project now get the permissions the umask gives any new file, such as `0644`. Before, several of them were readable only by the user who ran pnpm, which broke Docker images that run as a different user [#​17435](https://redirect.github.com/orgs/pnpm/discussions/17435).

  The fix applies to:

  - `node_modules/.pnpm-workspace-state-v1.json`. A different user running `pnpm run` reinstalled the dependencies because it could not read this file.
  - `pnpm-workspace.yaml`
  - the files written by `pnpm deploy`
  - patch files from `pnpm patch-commit`
  - the lockfile restored by `pnpm dedupe --check`
  - the Cargo and Python files that pnpm writes

  When pnpm edits an existing file, the file keeps its permissions.

- `pnpm install` no longer writes broken dependency links when the project's `node_modules` is a symlink to another directory, such as another project's `node_modules`. The install reported success, but the links it wrote did not resolve [#​17448](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17448).

- Commands installed with `pnpm add --global` now find the dependencies that pnpm hoists for their package. A package that loads a dependency it does not declare, such as a native addon's platform-specific package, failed with "Cannot find module". Reinstall such a package with `pnpm add --global` to update its existing command [#​17503](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17503).

- When pnpm switches to the version a project pins, it now installs that version's native binary for the current host, even if the project's `supportedArchitectures` excludes the host. Before, pnpm could not use the pinned version and kept running the installed one. pnpm also repairs a pinned version that an earlier install left without the host's binary.

- With the global virtual store, a change to a dependency of one package in a dependency cycle now gives every package in that cycle a new directory. Before, the other packages kept their directories and still linked the old copy of the changed package, so the project could load two copies of it [#​17466](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17466).

  Packages in a dependency cycle, and packages that depend on one, move to new global virtual store directories once after this update. Those that run a build miss the side-effects cache once.

- With `nodeLinker: hoisted`, when two workspace projects need the same package version and it cannot be hoisted to the root, each project now keeps the copy installed in its own `node_modules`. Build scripts run in each of these copies. Before, the second project's copy was replaced with a symlink to the first project's, so every repeat install imported it again [#​17498](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17498).

- The Node.js `latest` selector now chooses the newest stable release [#​17490](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17490).

- Hardlinking from the store now stats each store file once per install. Since pnpm 12.8.0, a store file was stat'ed again for every package that links it. On an offline install of a large workspace, that added up to 15% system CPU [#​17500](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17500).

##### Repeat installs and local dependencies

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` no longer reports an outdated lockfile right after the install that wrote it. This happened when a pnpmfile `readPackage` hook or `packageExtensions` changed the dependencies or peer dependencies of a local directory dependency outside the workspace projects. It affected a `file:` dependency, an injected `workspace:../dir` dependency outside the workspace patterns, and an injected workspace package left out by `--filter` [#​17447](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17447) [#​17473](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17473).

  A repeat `pnpm install` now takes the fast path when `ignoredOptionalDependencies` removes an optional dependency of a `file:` directory dependency. It used to resolve again on every run.

- `pnpm install` now resolves again after an edit to an injected `workspace:../dir` dependency outside the workspace patterns under a shared lockfile. It used to keep the lockfile unchanged. The next `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` then failed [#​17476](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17476).

- `pnpm install` now resolves a local directory again after its `package.json` changes when an override or a package extension adds it to the dependencies of a registry package. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` fails on a lockfile that still records the old dependencies of such a directory [#​17486](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17486).

- With `injectWorkspacePackages` and per-project lockfiles, `pnpm install` now updates a project's lockfile when a local tarball that an injected workspace project depends on is replaced. The project's lockfile kept the old version and integrity before.

- `pnpm install` now detects a change to a local tarball or directory that only a pnpmfile `readPackage` hook depends on. A repeat install reported "Already up to date" and kept the old contents before [pnpm/tasks#227](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/227).

- `pnpm install` now relinks a `workspace:` or `link:` dependency whose link was deleted from `node_modules`. It used to report "Already up to date" and leave the link missing [#​17485](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17485).

- A repeat `pnpm install` reports "Already up to date" again when a pnpmfile `readPackage` hook changes the dependencies of a workspace project. Since 12.15.0, every such install ran in full [#​17468](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17468).

  After an edit to a project's `package.json`, `pnpm install` and `verifyDepsBeforeRun` now run the pnpmfile's `readPackage` hook on the edited manifest before comparing it with the lockfile. They could report the project up to date when the hook rewrote the edited dependency to a specifier the lockfile did not record.

##### Adding and updating dependencies

- `pnpm update --latest` with package selectors now updates the dependencies of the selected packages within their declared ranges. Excluded packages and their dependencies keep their locked versions [#​17444](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17444).

- `pnpm add <pkg>@<tag>` now uses a catalog entry set to that same dist-tag. The dependency is saved as `catalog:` and the entry stays as written [pnpm/tasks#225](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/225).

  When `pnpm add` adds a new dist-tag such as `vue@legacy` to a catalog, the catalog entry records the exact version the tag points to. The same applies to a dependency added without a version when the `tag` setting names a dist-tag other than `latest`.

- `pnpm add` now saves the resolved version range of an npm alias. For example, `pnpm add v2@npm:vue` and `pnpm add v2@npm:vue@^3.0.0` both save `npm:vue@^3.5.13`.

##### Running scripts and commands

- Programs that a script or `pnpm exec` command leaves running, such as a browser opened by the `open` package, now outlive pnpm exactly when they would outlive the command run without pnpm. Before, on Windows, a failed command, `Ctrl+C`, or a closed terminal ended all of them. pnpm still ends them when it is killed or crashes.

  When a recursive or parallel run bails, the scripts still running now receive `SIGTERM` on Unix and are killed only if they are still running two seconds later. On Windows, everything those scripts started is ended, including detached processes whose parent has already exited. Before, a bail killed them at once [#​17465](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17465).

- On Windows, the shell shim of a `.cmd` or `.bat` bin now runs it under Git Bash when MSYS argument conversion is off, such as with `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` or `MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL='*'`. The shim used to start an interactive cmd.exe prompt [#​17480](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17480).

- `pnx` and `pnpm create` now run the command in the directory selected by `--dir` or `--workspace-root`. Without either flag, the command still runs in the directory pnpm was started in.

- `pnpm --env-file` now reads files the way `node --env-file` does. Values are taken as written, so `$VAR` is no longer expanded and Windows paths such as `C:\Users\me` load unchanged. A file is no longer rejected for its contents.

##### Settings and messages

- `pnpm version` no longer creates a git commit and tag when `gitTagVersion` is set to `false` [#​17460](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17460).

- `pnpm publish` now reads the `publishBranch` setting from `pnpm-workspace.yaml` and from `PNPM_CONFIG_PUBLISH_BRANCH`. The `--publish-branch` flag overrides it.

- `pnpm` now accepts `--strict-ssl` and `--local-address <ip>` on the command line.

- `pnpm doctor` uses a 15-second timeout when checking registry connectivity.

- `pnpm-workspace.yaml` parse errors now report `ERR_PNPM_INVALID_SETTING`.

- The error for a dependency with an invalid name in a project's manifest now names the project's directory. It used to say only "The current package", which did not tell which workspace project to fix [#​17475](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17475).

Issues.Title: fix(material/datepicker): improve comparison-range colour in docs example
Issues.Body:
Fixes #31663

The comparison-range example uses `tertiary-container` as its background in M3, 
which is nearly identical to `primary-container` in several themes (e.g. Azure & Blue). 
The two overlapping campaign date ranges become visually indistinguishable.

**Fix:** Override two CSS custom properties scoped to the example host element with 
an amber tint — the same colour Material 2 used — so the visual distinction is clear 
in every M3 theme. No effect on user apps.

Issues.Title: fix(aria/accordion): avoid errors when destroyed before initialization
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Fixes #34060.

`AccordionTrigger.ngOnDestroy()` reads the required `panel()` input even if the trigger is destroyed before the first change detection and `ngOnInit` has not run. Destroying a newly created TestBed fixture therefore throws NG0950, despite the template binding `[panel]` correctly.

Retain the panel associated during `ngOnInit` and only clear that association during destruction if initialization established it. Unregistering from the group remains safe for an unregistered trigger. This follows the registration/cleanup approach in https://github.com/angular/components/pull/33974 (combobox).

Adds an early-destruction regression test and an initialized control that verifies the panel association exists before destruction and is cleared afterward. The changes are based on main after https://github.com/angular/components/pull/34053.

Related Tree PR: https://github.com/angular/components/pull/34059. This PR is independent and contains only accordion changes.

## Validation

- Before the fix, the Chromium accordion suite reports **44 passed, 1 failed**; the new early-destruction test throws `NG0950: Input "panel" is required but no value is available yet.` The initialized control passes.
- After the fix, `pnpm test src/aria/accordion --no-watch` passes: **45 specs, 0 failures**, including the strengthened initialized cleanup assertion.
- `pnpm bazelisk test //goldens:aria_api` passes.
- `pnpm ng-dev format changed --check` passes.
- TSLint passes for both changed TypeScript files.
- `git diff --check` and commit-message validation pass.

Tested with Node.js 22.23.4 and pnpm 12.16.1 on macOS arm64. The full Material/CDK/Aria test suites and Firefox were not run locally. Complete reproduction code, steps, environment, and actual error are in #34060.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(aria/accordion): avoid errors when destroyed before initialization" (#34061)

Issues.Title: fix(aria/tree): avoid errors when destroyed before initialization
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Fixes #34058.

`TreeItem` and `TreeItemGroup` read required signal inputs during destruction, even when they are destroyed before the first change detection and `ngOnInit` has not run. A synchronously destroyed TestBed fixture therefore throws NG0950 for `parent` or `ownedBy`, despite the inputs being bound in its template.

Retain the tree, parent group, and owning item used during registration. Destruction only unregisters those retained references, so uninitialized directives have nothing to clean up. This follows the registration/cleanup approach used for combobox in https://github.com/angular/components/pull/33974 (related issue https://github.com/angular/components/issues/33972).

Adds regression tests for a static flat tree and a static nested tree destroyed before their first change detection, plus controls that destroy both after initialization. This PR only changes tree; no accordion changes or public API changes are included.

## Validation

- Before the fix, the Chromium tree suite reports **144 passed, 2 failed**: the new early-destruction tests throw NG0950 for `parent` and `ownedBy`. Both initialized controls pass.
- After the fix, `pnpm test src/aria/tree --no-watch` passes: **146 specs, 0 failures**.
- `pnpm bazelisk test //goldens:aria_api` passes.
- `pnpm ng-dev format changed --check` passes.
- TSLint passes for the three changed TypeScript files.
- `git diff --check` passes.

Tested with Node.js 22.23.4 and pnpm 12.16.1 on macOS arm64. The full Material/CDK/Aria test suites and Firefox were not run locally; validation covers the Chromium tree suite and Aria API golden check. Detailed reproduction code, setup, and actual errors are in #34058.

Issues.Title: bug(material/select): mat-select option is not announced on the very first time options are visible
Issues.Body: 1. ### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version ### The previous version in which this bug was not present was _No response_ ### Description When a `mat-select` has an initial value (for example, set through a reactive form control) and the user opens it for the first time, the screen reader reads the active option's text but does not announce it as "selected". If the user moves to different options and returns back to the selected one, the same option is announced correctly as "selected". ### Reproduction StackBlitz link: https://stackblitz.com/edit/3j8yhubg?file=src%2Fexample%2Fselect-reactive-form-example.ts Steps to reproduce: 1. Create a mat-select bound to a reactive FormControl with an initial value: 2. Turn on a screen reader (VoiceOver). 3. Tab to the select and open it with Space, Enter or Alt+Down 4. Listen to the announcement for the highlighted option. 5. Go to next option. 6. Return to previous option and listen to the announcement. "Selected" is announced for the option which is selected. ### Expected Behavior "Selected" should be announced on the very first time the panel of options open. ### Actual Behavior "Selected" is not announce on the very first time the panel opens and the user is on the selected item. It is announced when the user goes to some different options and returns to the selected item. ### Environment - Angular: 21.2.22 - CDK/Material: 21.2.14 - Browser(s): Chrome - Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): MacOS

Issues.Title: fix(material/select): prevent option selection while disabled
Issues.Body:
Follow-up to #34044 with the corrected, fully styled reproduction. The earlier recording was missing structural styles; the video below uses the official theme and shows the parent Select becoming disabled before the option is clicked.

## Problem

I was playing around with `mat-select` and noticed a bug where:

1. Open an enabled Select.
2. Set `disabled` to `true` while its panel is open.
3. Click an option. The selected value changes and `selectionChange` fires.

Here is a reproduction video of the issue, recorded before the fix:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0bd6a927-7f4c-4271-9227-0de589eb8b7c

This uses published Angular Material 21.2.14, the official Azure Blue prebuilt theme, and a standard `mat-form-field`. Click "Disable in 3 seconds", open the Select, and wait for the field to turn gray before clicking Orange. The readout shows that the parent is disabled before the selection. There are no forced clicks or custom select, option, or overlay styles.

The original recording was missing styles, which made the issue unclear. I agree that an individually disabled option already has `pointer-events: none`. This is a different state: the parent Select becomes disabled after opening, while its options are still enabled. In the corrected reproduction, an option has `aria-disabled="false"` and `pointer-events: auto`, even though its parent Select reports `aria-disabled="true"`.

A prop update can send `disabled=true` while someone is choosing an option, for example when an asynchronous request completes or a timer fires. I ran into this sequence while varying component props with Hegel and exercising UI actions with Bombadil in Anta, then reproduced the Angular Material behavior independently with Playwright.

My first thought was to close the panel, since that is what I observed with a native HTML `select` in Chromium. The [HTML option-picking algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-elements.html#concept-select-pick) also stops without selecting an option when the select is disabled.

This PR takes the smaller step of rejecting user selection when the parent Select is disabled. It preserves the current panel behavior and still allows programmatic value changes. Closing the panel when disabled is a reasonable choice too, and I'm happy to adjust the PR to follow Angular Material's preferred pattern. The behavior I'm trying to guarantee is simply that a disabled Select stops accepting user selections.

## Validation

- The regression fails on the original source in Chromium and Firefox.
- `pnpm exec bazel test //src/material/select:unit_tests --test_output=errors`: Chromium and Firefox targets pass with the fix.
- Rechecked the styled browser reproduction: the enabled field turns gray, the parent reports disabled, and a normal click on Orange still changes the value and emits one `selectionChange` before the fix. No page errors.
- Current upstream `MatOption._selectViaInteraction()` still checks only the option's own disabled state.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(material/select): prevent option selection while disabled" (#34056)
